events.summary: In the 1960s, biologists introduced wolves to Coronation Island in Alaska after deer overran it and decimated the forest understory. The wolves ate all the deer and, with nothing left to eat, starved. About 50 years later, the wolves of Pleasant Island Alaska found themselves in a similar situation: living on an island in the Pacific with no deer left to eat. The wolves of Pleasant Island, however, have not died out. Instead, theyve broadened their palate to include sea otters. What scientists dont know is how widespread this surf-and-turf phenomenon is. How does the complex web of wolf, deer, sea otter, hundreds of islands and a massive logging industry interact? In 2024, a rescued border collie named Barley joined the investigation. Employ

events.title: The Innocents: social justice advocacy through performance art

events.summary: What if the person you hope to save becomes a mirror of everything you have lost? Óscar Restrepo is an aging, erratic poet whose devotion to literature has brought neither recognition nor stability. He sees a chance at redemption in Yurlady, a gifted teenager from a working-class Medellín neighborhood, and appoints himself her mentor. But his intentions soon collide with his ego, social inequality, and an artistic establishment hungry for new voices. Shot on textured 16mm film and anchored by Ubeimar Ríos’s remarkable performance, A POET moves between satire, tenderness, and discomfort. Winner of the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize at Cannes, it is a sharply observed tragicomedy about failure, class, mentorship, and art. Why We Chose This Film

Drawing on the visual techniques of sumi-e ink painting, the five sets of photographs express seasonality through portraiture, gesture, everyday objects, and atmosphere. At the same time, the artists are exploring the relationship between tradition and cultural identity as Japanese and multi-heritage Japanese artists living in Oregon, superimposing one of the most prevalent motifs in Japanese art onto a new context. events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. Plan your visit and explore the exhibition: worldforestry.org/lookout-landscape

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: The awesome destructive power of volcanoes, earthquakes, and tornadoes is examined as scientists seek to understand how these natural disasters are triggered and what can be done to minimize their deadly effects. Combining striking archival footage with computer-created reenactments and interviews, the film's sequence on volcanoes is centered on the massive Soufriere Hills eruption of 1995. A tremor in Izmit, Turkey - which cost the lives of 17,000 - sets the stage for the segment on earthquakes, while Dr. Joshua Wurman leads a group of "storm chasers" as the filmmakers investigate tornadoes. Kevin Bacon narrates this National Geographic Society production.

events.summary: Come enjoy Leslie McMillan’s one-of-a-kind handcrafted jewelry and painter bd dombrowsky’s visual explorations of the mischievous silver night and the many insights the capricious muse offers. Painter bd dombrowsky My visual style is derived from an interest in vintage illustrated books -- encyclopedias, primers, comics, and stories-- all the simple visual devices we use as a culture to educate and socialize ourselves. Much of my work is informed by myths and folklore as I relate our old stories and weave them into new stories. Using my background in drama, sculpture and printmaking, my goal is to craft a resonant space in which these stories are allowed to unfold, drawn from our shared mythos but reimagined by me and narrated by the viewer themselves. Jewelry Artist Leslie McMillan As a jewelry smith I am all over the place. To begin with I have ADHD, so my mind is manic. I roam from fusing gold on steel to traditional silversmithing to bonding Japanese silver leaf. When working with steel and gold, I am drawn to the truth that you cannot control the outcome. By heating the gold high enough to fuse with the steel, it takes on a life of its own and travels where it wants to go. When approaching sterling silver and natural stones, I follow a more traditional method. Creating hand-forged settings and sourcing stones from First Nation lapidary artists are fundamental to my work. No matter the process, I rely on inspiration from the great Pacific Northwest and all its natural beauty to influence my final piece. October 29 through November 23, 11am-7pm Last Thursday Opening Reception, October 29, 6-9pm
events.title: Moonlight Mischief: Jewelry and Paintings

events.summary: This exhibition highlights a distinct artistic collaboration between printmakers Cassie Ferguson and Charlie Cohan, marking the creative intersection of their independent yet interrelated studios, Lost Bearings Press (LBP) and BurnPrint Studio (BPS). Centered on a shared dedication to traditional printmaking, the showcase features a diverse range of techniques, including stone lithography, screen printing, polyester plate lithography, and relief printmaking. The conceptual foundation of this exhibition hinges on a collaborative print created by Cohan and Ferguson in 2017, which juxtaposed the iconic Burnside Skatepark with an urban overpass. This visual conversation continues in Ferguson’s ongoing series of stone lithographs capturing DIY skateparks. Her work seeks to honor and archive the subcultural spaces that have shaped her lived experience. Because these grassroots spaces often thrive under overpasses and within neglected industrial zones, her prints seamlessly connect with Cohan’s imagery of Portland’s monumental bridges. Together, the artists offer a multifaceted view of the city, championing the gritty beauty of structural environments. Their works invite viewers to reflect on their own relationship to the municipal landscape and to find new ways of seeing everyday urban scenes. Additionally, the exhibition introduces recent work by Nakemiah “Kiki” Williams, produced in collaboration with Ferguson and Cohan at LBP and BPS. This project marks the debut publication for LBP and brings their history full circle, as both Williams and Ferguson are alumnae of Cohan’s printmaking program at the University of Hawai’i at Mānoa. This collaboration marks the beginning of collaborative print work at LBP, which is now open for publishing and contracted prints of primarily stone lithographs.
events.title: Under the Overpass

Each session weaves together horticulture, tea culture, and botanical art in a relaxed, welcoming setting: Learn the plant up close: A Lan Su gardener leads a close-up botanical show-and-tell, sharing seasonal plant facts, cultural stories, and growing insights. Taste the season: Enjoy a sampling of seasonal teas from Yun Shui Teahouse. Create botanical art: An OBA artist guides a full botanical art class inspired by the featured plant. Whether you’re returning to Steep & Paint or joining for the first time, this refreshed program offers an even richer way to experience Lan Su. Under this alias he has released 6 LPs and toured the world at venues such as the Newport Folk Festival and San Francisco's Great American Music Hall. Geer's music has been featured on AMC, NPR, WFMU and SiriusXM. 2022 finds Drunken Prayer touring across the US out of north Mississippi with members of the Drive By Truckers, Squirrel Nut Zippers, and the Jimbo Mathus band. On the side Geer is the lead guitar player for alt-country goths Freakwater and writes for other musicians such as the Brooklyn rock and soul artist Bette Smith. events.summary: New Room Studios is proud to present this Portland debut show by the Genius Artist Fellow and matter painter Jeff Beers. “Paper & Raincoat” are the two main ingredients of a new series that unfolds like a myth cycle of life and death. Beers painstakingly made it out of scraps of thin sheets of paper that he’s aged for 30 years, and surplus raincoat material from Columbia Sportswear. \(Beers got the latter from the local nonprofit SCRAP Creative Reuse.\) After 16 months of meticulous work, these two simple ingredients have found cosmic depths in this series of 8 pieces. The show also includes a series of Beers’ earlier, more earthy and elemental works. These pieces use tars, paints, emulsions and waxes to explore simultaneously the microcosms and macrocosms of the materials. Rarely able to afford art supplies, Beers \(newrooms.org/artists/jeff-beers\) learned at an early age how to make his own. He still makes his own paints and emulsions, and his subject matter is often the materials that he’s foraged from the built environment and from the natural environment. He works with the materials until he learns their languages and how they want to see, and much of his art is in the discipline of letting them speak through him. Beers was awarded a 2025-2026 Genius Artist Fellowship by New Room Studios \(newrooms.org\). This program recognizes and supports artists who have a history of making excellent work over the years, despite significant barriers. As part of his Fellowship, New Room Studios is producing this show. This show is hosted by The Salmonberry Trail Foundation \(salmonberrytrail.org\), which is dedicated to building an 82-mile trail for hiking and biking from Banks to the Oregon Coast. “Jeff Beers: Paper & Raincoat” will take over their spacious and historic office in downtown Portland in November.
events.title: Jeff Beers: Paper & Raincoat

events.summary: The fierce warrior Kwa must take Elān’s place in their ongoing battle against the invading Koosh, in The Eagle in the Mountain \(Solaris\), the thrilling sequel to Caskey Russell’s The Door on the Sea! Elān’s life changed forever when the loud-mouthed raven chose him to go on a journey to save his people. Now returned from his quest, Elān is changed, withdrawn — and will not touch the weapon he is destined to wield. Raven knows that Elān must take up the weapon for his people, or cast it back into the Koosh world through the Door. But Elān will not budge. The invading Koosh loom ever closer, and Elān’s people have no hero to fight for them. So raven turns to Kwa, Elān’s sour yet tough companion. Kwa is determined to prove herself, doing whatever it takes to become the warrior leader her people need her to be. With Chetdyl the wolf by her side, she prepares an attack against the Koosh. But she knows that what she really needs is the weapon Elān refuses to use. If he won’t use it, she will. But the weapon will not bow to her — unless she does as raven says and pushes Elān through the Door herself. Russell will be joined in conversation by Lara Messersmith-Glavin, author of Ruiner. Buy the book: https://www.powells.com/events/caskey-russell-9781837867400

events.summary: Ana Maria Spagna’s new collection, Coiled: Essays on Urgency and Kinship \(Bison Books\), covers eight years of unrest, personal and communal, beginning with stubborn patriotic certainty, a faith in neighborliness and American ideals, and ending with something broader: an alliance with the matriarch, Mother Nature, and the ways she elides ideology or definition. The essays shift perspective to focus on subjects too often overlooked: unwritten histories of xenophobia in the American West, the rights of rivers everywhere, queerness in middle age, troubled human kin, and our more-than-human kin — snakes, fish, bears, sea lions, and a beloved robotic cat. These essays balance wonder at the world around us and urgency at the threats to it, but they add one more imperative: to focus on kinship — on the people we care for and those who care for us, and the more-than-human too. Spagna will be joined in conversation by Michelle Nijhuis, author of Beloved Beasts. Buy the book: https://www.powells.com/events/ana-maria-spagna-9781496248817
events.title: Powell's Presents: Ana Maria Spagna in Conversation With Michelle Nijhuis

events.summary: BOLD is thrilled to host a reading an anthology reading for *Constellations: Selected Tales from Muslim Storytellers.* Join Muslim storytellers as we relay tales of family, community, and explore belonging. This anthology was inspired by 13th century poet Jalāl al-Dīn Muḥammad Rūmī, who says, "Do not feel lonely. There is an entire universe within you." You will hear tales of celestial bodies, dark matter, and earthbound aliens. Space cats, telescopes, and international space stations are within reach, as these authors show. Niyyah Ruscher-Haqq (she/her/hers) writes fantasy and predominantly horror. Her novella, The Veil, debuted September 2026. Niyyah has published several short stories and was selected as 2026 We Need Diverse Books Mentee for her middle grade fantasy manuscript “Under.” She serves as Secretary for mīzān, and as co-chair for Young Willamette Writers. mohammad borhan ortega-allam (he/him/his) is the founder and facilitator of the workshop series Yallah! Muslims Write for Literary Arts and President of mīzān, a nonprofit dedicated to self-identifying Muslim writers. A participant in the 2025 Tin House Summer Workshop, he is hard at work on his debut novel. Yousuf Azhar was born in India and raised in California. He holds a Memoir Writing Certificate from Stanford Continuing Studies, studied flash fiction at the Kenyon Review Writers Workshop, and is pursuing a writing certificate at the University of Iowa. His work appears in Tasbih, Threads at Cal, and Constellations. myrah rafi'ah beverly (she/her/hers) is an African-American and Malay writer from Park City, Illinois. Alhumdulilah, she has a bachelor’s degree in Comparative Cultures and Politics from Michigan State University. She has designed and self-published two poetry zines: Eat, Sleep, Pray, and Just Forget and I Will Survive in Times 100. Aminat Matemilola is a fiction-writer based Burlington, MA. She is a keen observer of nature and adventurer who finds joy in counting her blessings and savoring life’s simple moments. Her writing explores personal transformation, family dynamics and the quiet resilience found in everyday experiences. Nazneen Khan makes her literary debut with Amaras Path in CONSTELLATIONS, a fiction anthology. A Commerce graduate writing from the PNW, she loves true stories and realistic fiction, finding inspiration in everyday moments. She enjoys photography, henna art, exploring nature and supporting local school programs. Zarmeena Riaz hopes to paint pictures with her words; vivid, authentic and full of heart. A full time mom, homemaker and home educator, things that intrigue her are far too many. While this is her first time publishing a short story, she hopes to one day author an international nonfiction bestseller. Asmaa Hashish’s love and passion for reading made it her favorite hobby—until she discovered writing. What began with diaries and an exploration of the psychology of life grew into crafting stories that explore human nature and the connections between us. “Untangled” is her first published short story. events.summary: internationally-renowned concert organist Nathan Laube presents an exciting recital of thrilling organ music from a wide variety of eras and locales. This one-of-a-kind program features a diverse selection of works by Felix Mendelssohn, Dieterich Buxtehude, Charles-Marie Widor, and more! Laube's 75-minute recital showcases both his dazzling technique and his profound gift of listening carefully to the instrument and eliciting from it a thrilling range of musical colors – a combination perfectly suited to the world-class Rosales organ. He'll explore the organ’s full range of tonal colors throughout the program, which is offered in celebration of the organ's 40th birthday this year. Nathan Laube, a truly generational talent of our time, is one of the world’s most elite organ performers and pedagogues. He is Associate Professor of Organ on the faculty of the Eastman School of Music in Rochester New York and International Consultant in Organ Studies at the Royal Birmingham Conservatoire in the United Kingdom. His extensive international recital career takes him continually to major concert venues and festivals around the world. Trinity's pipe organ, built by Manuel Rosales and installed in 1986, is one of the finest pipe organs in North America. We celebrate its 40th anniversary this year with a series of concerts and events: trinity-episcopal.org/rosales-organ. Trinity Music is the professional music program of Trinity Episcopal Cathedral, comprising the Cathedral Schola, Trinity Choir, and Choir School, a concert series with nationally recognized guest artists, and the acclaimed Rosales organ, all in one of Portland's finest acoustic spaces.
events.title: Celebrity Organ Recital: Nathan Laube

events.summary: Every so often, you’re sitting at a bus stop or browsing at the cheese counter, and you stumble into an interaction. For a moment, you connect with a random person, having a brief conversation you didn’t know was coming. You get a glimpse of a world recombined into something foreign but familiar. Through that chance encounter and surprise conversation, you might find yourself reminded of other ways to live your own life. Life Recording — Live! illuminates the worlds of the people in the audience that night. Each month, interviewer Leif Olsen leverages their playfulness and curiosity to encourage a few members of the audience to talk about themselves for a while. The remaining audience listens and learns from the gems and insights of people living lives different from their own. Next time you find yourself out in the world of strangers, you might look for storytellers instead. Meet the team: Leif Olsen, The Life Recording Company, has been working with audio for a decade and has over 1.92 million views on their work across platforms. Leif has a Master's in Multimedia Journalism and has been recording people's life stories since 2019. Check out their work or book a life recording session at theliferecording.com Brandon Giles, is a producer and strategic planner who turns ambitious ideas into retreats, workshops, and events that engage people in inclusive, immersive ways. Through their business, LB Collaborations, Brandon facilitates collaboration for individuals and teams. Currently taking on new collaborations and strategic planning projects for fall 2026–more at bytheLB.Co Social Good Place offers co-working memberships, event spaces, and community events to create positive experiences and influences in our world. We also offer a pathway to fiscal sponsorship for charitable initiatives through our parent organization, Social Good Fund. Learn more at SocialGoodPlace.org Accessibility Note: Social Good Place is housed in a historic building with significant physical limitations. There is no level entry to the building, no ramps, and no elevators. Accessing the event space requires navigating stairs. You can read Social Good Place's full statement on accessibility at socialgoodplace.org.

events.summary: The Breaks Roberts • Walter • Moore When three modern groove masters of modern funk and soul-jazz converge, sparks are bound to fly. The Breaks brings together guitarist Eddie Roberts (The New Mastersounds), drummer Stanton Moore (Galactic), and organist Robert Walter (The Greyboy Allstars)—three musicians whose collective groove has shaped the sound of contemporary funk for over two decades. Rooted in the tradition of late-’60s organ trios and hard-hitting boogaloo, The Breaks pushes the sound forward with deep-pocket rhythms, tight arrangements, and fearless improvisation. Eddie Roberts’ sharp, melodic guitar work dances effortlessly over Stanton Moore’s explosive New Orleans-infused drum grooves, while Robert Walter’s signature Hammond organ tones tie it all together with grit and soul. Between them, they’ve logged countless tours, recorded landmark albums, and collaborated with a who’s-who of the modern jam, funk, and jazz worlds. But in The Breaks, the chemistry feels spontaneous—three kindred spirits locking into a groove and letting it ride. From sweaty club sets to major festival stages, The Breaks deliver a sound that’s both deeply rooted and constantly evolving—a raw, joyful celebration of rhythm and musical conversation.
events.title: The Breaks - Roberts • Walter • Moore

events.summary: From bayou kitchens to front porches, this captivating play celebrates the heart, humor, and resilience of Louisiana's women. Pull up a chair and savor a celebration of the remarkable women whose strength and spirit have always been the secret ingredient in Louisiana’s gumbo. This show is for you if you’ve ever wondered… Where do I belong? Where is home? What is a Cajun? What’s a Creole? Are they more than just styles of cooking? How different are Southerners from Northwesterners? How do you make a roux? What’s Mardi Gras all about anyway? What’s the deal with New Orleans and voodoo, vampires, and above ground graves? How do you “laissez les bon temps rouler”? Can you be both proud and ashamed of where you come from? How do you pronounce geaux, lagniappe, Ouachita, Tchoupitoulas, or couillon? Do you know what it means to miss New Orleans? Shelley Tate's one-woman show developed as an ensemble piece: a 90-minute show about history and culture of Louisiana —served with heart, humor, and just the right amount of spice. The gumbo is rich, the laughter is loud, and the women are unforgettable. GUMBO "...a steel magnolia in the Rose City" Performs Fridays & Saturdays at 7:30pm and Sunday at 2:00pm, November 6-15th, 2026. Tickets $15 at Magentatheater.com.

events.summary: Free Community Concert Doors open 7:00pm - Show starts 7:30pm The United States Air Force Band of the Golden West is stationed in the San Francisco Bay Area at Travis Air Force Base. The only active-duty Air Force band west of the Rockies, the band is composed of 60 talented and versatile Airman-musicians forming a concert band, jazz band, rock band, and many classical chamber groups. In addition to performing for civilian communities throughout the states of California, Washington, Oregon, Arizona, and Nevada, the band supports 13 Air Force Bases, 8 Air Force Reserve Wings, and 6 recruiting squadrons in over 250 annual performances for audiences totaling 7 million. The Band of the Golden West has performed for gubernatorial inaugurations, with guest artists such as Marvin Stamm, Arturo Sandoval, Bob Hope, and for the fans of San Francisco Giants, Sacramento Kings, and the San Francisco 49ers. In 2023, the Band was honored to perform for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting hosted by President Joe Biden in San Francisco and attended by dozens of presidents and prime ministers from around the world. More recent events include featured performances with the Los Angeles Philharmonic, San Francisco Symphony, and the Tournament of Roses Parade. The Clarinet Trio are part of the United States Air Force Band of the Golden West from Travis Air Force Base, California. This group supports a wide variety of musical events ranging from military ceremonies and patriotic shows to educational programs and recitals, excelling at all styles of music including marches, jazz, and classical. As part of the Band of the Golden West, the mission of group is to harness musical excellence to HONOR our nation and those who have served, INSPIRE patriotism and resilience in our Airmen, Guardians, and nations’ citizens, and CONNECT the Air Force with the American public and community partners. The excellence demonstrated by the Clarinet Trio reflects the excellence displayed by all Airmen stationed worldwide, whose selfless service and sacrifices ensure the freedoms enjoyed by citizens of the United States of America.
events.title: United States Air Force Presents: Band of the Golden West - Clarinet Trio

events.summary: Do You Feel Anger? lives in the familiar world of water coolers, staplers, and office conference rooms — but Nelson-Greenberg's language quickly reveals something far stranger underneath. When Sofia, an empathy coach, arrives at a debt collection agency as part of a lawsuit settlement, she finds a workplace where toxic masculinity has so thoroughly warped the atmosphere that even the most basic concepts — feelings, empathy, basic human decency — have become alien and absurd. The play is laugh-out-loud funny, populated by an unusual cast of characters whose skewed logic and bizarre non-sequiturs mask something genuinely unsettling. What emerges from the sensitivity training sessions is not reform, but a portrait of how pervasive and deeply embedded the patriarchy can be — and how it distorts everyone it touches, including those trying to resist it.
events.title: PSU Theater Arts Presents: Do You Feel Anger?

events.title: Wizard of Floyd

events.summary: Marsha Blovotnik is angry. So angry! The whole world is *fakakte*, but for this Leftie Jewish Lesbian, it’s her sister Janice who really burns her *tuchus*. Janice invites herself over for *Shabbos* dinner and then shows up three minutes early. Who does that?!? Just before her sister arrives, a mysterious ancestor gives Marsha a pot of magical chicken soup with the power to cure the world of its woes — if only Marsha can cool down enough to share a bowl of soup with her sister. A buoyant, crackling comedy about how to live in a dumpster fire.
events.title: Marsha Blovotnik and the Marvelous Magical Chicken Soup

events.summary: At a time when many theatres are closing their doors or reducing programming, 100 Lives Repertory in Portland’s Buckman neighborhood is celebrating the inaugural season in its brand-new space. And the first play is a doozy: a sleek, sly, sci-fi mystery titled Anthropology, penned by Lauren Gunderson, one of America’s most produced playwrights. Anthropology is about a grieving computer coder, Merril, who builds an AI replica of her missing and presumed dead sister. Adding to the loss, Merril’s relationship with her girlfriend has come to an end, which draws her deeper and deeper into her ‘project’ of bringing back a version of her sister, to help heal her grief and lessen her loneliness. This is the Oregon premiere of Anthropology which had its world debut in London at Hampstead Theatre in 2023. The play runs Thursday through Sunday from October 23 through November 15. It features an all-female, four-actor cast and is directed by 100 Lives Rep’s Executive Director Cat Plein. Due to nudity and sexual situations, it is recommended only for adult audiences.
events.title: Anthropology

events.summary: Robert Ellis has named his new album after himself and the reason is clear. The album is both his most personal statement yet and a summation of his career thus far. Robert Ellis opens with “Perfect Strangers,” a meditation on what brings people together \(and how tenuous that connection can be\), and ends with “It's Not OK,” a raw look at emotional compromise. Between those two powerful bookends are nine other songs that set Ellis's soaring vocals and knowing melodies against his sharp, dark observations, and that show him in full command of a vibrant set of songwriting skills—irony, distance, character, narrative, a thoughtful relationship between sound and sense. Ellis was born and raised in Lake Jackson, a town about an hour from Houston whose other famous residents have included the Pauls \(Ron and Rand\) and Selena \(the original Queen of Tejano, not the current pop sensation\). From an early age, he escaped small-town boredom through music. At first, his tastes ran toward traditional hits. “I remember having a bunch of pop records when I was really young: No Doubt and Michael Jackson and Garth Brooks. That was when I was pretty passive as a listener—I liked them, but maybe I got to them because my mom or one of my sisters had them. The first I really got obsessed with was a Doc Watson collection. I was already starting to play guitar, and my uncle told my mom to get it for me. He was my first guitar hero.” As he developed as a writer, though, he found himself drawn toward the smartest and sharpest of the class of songwriters who developed in the 1970s: artists like Paul Simon, John Prine, and Randy Newman. And he didn’t just listen to them. He learned from them. Specifically, he learned the finer points of songcraft. “I've been a big fan of Paul Simon for a long time,” he says. “He has this capacity to surprise you with his music and his lyrics. With John Prine's songs, I grew from believing that they happened to him to understanding that it didn’t matter if they really happened to him. And Randy Newman? Wow. I especially love a record like Trouble in Paradise, when there are all these artificial 1980s production techniques, but they’re being used in the service of this master composer.” That respect for tradition—but more specifically for the fact that so-called traditional artists were in fact consistent risk-takers—fuel Ellis’s new record. “With this record,” he says, “I feel like I’ve gotten to where I can use the material of my own life as a jumping-off point. But now I can do different things with that material.” In this case, of course, the material has an element of melancholy. Much of the record revolves around the dissolution of Ellis’s marriage. It’s a breakup album, but not one that dissects its subject with straightforward rage and regret—Ellis and his ex-wife remain friends, and she is even featured in the album art, which was created after the divorce. Rather, it’s an album that finds Ellis reaching back into the trick bags of masters like Simon, Prine, and Newman, and employing the full complement of skills that he’s learned from them. “‘Perfect Strangers,’ took a month,” he says. “I had a notepad and walked around New York, giving myself personal therapy through the eyes of the city.” Other songs came faster. “I wrote ‘Elephant” quickly,” he says. “It's about my misunderstanding of monogamy and my complete bewilderment with some of the ideas that I grew up with. I felt that in the past year, lots of constructs I took for granted were turned on their head. But I was careful to express those ideas in a way where the gray areas got to stay gray. If what you’re saying is that you’re confused, you shouldn't say you're confused. You should betray a contradiction.” Ellis isn’t afraid of sophistication. The beautifully orchestrated “You’re Not the One” has more complex origins than its title might suggest. “For that one, I woke up from a nightmare that was a kind of sex dream. In the dream, the faces around me kept changing. It was very eerie, like a David Lynch movie. The song has that sense of unease but also this Ellington bridge that’s unrelated to the key of the song. I’m really proud of that one.” But he can make his point with simplicity also, as in the chorus to “Drivin’,” a co-write with Angaleena Presley: “This don’t feel like living, it’s just surviving / I’m ain’t going nowhere, I’m just driving.” And then there’s “High Road,” the emotional center of the record, co-written with friend Jonny Fritz, a song about professional and personal insecurity that builds from lonesome shivers to almost operatic melodrama—all the while riding a lovely, fragile melody. While Ellis wrote nine of the album’s songs, he is also a generous collaborator dedicated to finding songs from other writers who advance his vision. “Once I knew that much of the record would be composed of these extremely personal songs like ‘Elephant’ or ‘High Road,’ but I was aware from the start that I couldn’t have a whole record of them. Putting it together was like assembling a collection of short stories. You need different tones and colors. So that’s why I included a song like ‘How I Love You,’ which was written by my friend Matt Vasquez, from Delta Spirit. We were hanging out, and I asked him if he had any good uptempo songs, and he showed me that one. And ‘Screw’ was written by Kelly Doyle, who plays guitar in our band. Listening to him work on his solo record, I was amazed by the sound. His process and palette were really inspirational to me.” The album ends with “It's Not OK,” which holds its ground as a traditional busted-love song before hurtling headlong into a dark thicket of guitars. “In that case, because the song is about that kind of emotional trouble, part of me that wanted dissonance and chaos. The melodic and rhythmic ideas to me are a different kind of information from the lyrics, but they’re still information.” As thoughtful as Ellis is about the process, his album also has plenty of pop pleasures. “California” is a jaunty, intimate travelogue that elevates into his chorus. “Amanda Jane” has an almost bossa nova shuffle and a melody that splits the difference between power pop and 70s soft rock. And “Couples Skate” reaches back even further. “I wrote that one while were on tour with Richard Thompson. It’s a green room song. I was just journaling, and I remembered holding this girl’s hand in second grade. It’s a nostalgic idea, which is why I reached for a 50s soul vibe. But it’s also nineties, in a way—something about it that reminds me of the rock and roll I was listening to around that time.” In the end, Robert Ellis \(the album\) is the most accurate reflection yet of Robert Ellis \(the man\). It’s analytical and emotional, calculated in spots and improvisational in others, restless, peaceful, never indifferent, never dispassionate. ROBERT ELLIS DISCOGRAPHY The Great Rearranger \(2009\) Photographs \(2011\) The Lights From The Chemical Plant \(2014\) Robert Ellis \(2016\)

With their audacious remixes such as Bel Mercy and My Humps appearing regularly in DJ sets by Hard Techno heavyweights including the likes of Ben Nicky, Nico Moreno, even extending to top-tier Bass acts such as Subtronics, BEAUZ also proved that Hard Techno can enjoy streaming appeal when their self-release “Ocho VIP” and “Lick It” became their hottest tracks on Spotify, with the former being played by Charlotte de Witte on Tomorrowland mainstage. Considering all their successes in 2024, it almost feels as if BEAUZ is destined to build their legacy on the realm of Hard Techno. With nearly a decade of studio experience experimenting with the art of genre amalgamation, their Hard Techno productions feel natural, intuitive, readily comprehensible, and are suitable for more than traditional warehouse rave and club environments. Besides maximizing their potential as artists, BEAUZ strive to ingrain their motto “BADDIE UP” within the minds of all their fans and the next generation of artists. The brothers exert themselves as leaders of positivity by regularly connecting with fans both online and offline after shows, living out their mission to elevate the realities of those around them.

events.summary: BOLD is thrilled to host a reading with Adam Oyster-Sands, author of We're doing pretty good if we can just get out alive, in conversation with Scott Cannon of Friendly Monster Press. Adam's first poetry chapbook, don’t call us punk because we hate that, was then released in 2024 through Steel Toe Books. Over the years, a number of Adam’s poems have been published by various literary journals and collections such as Picture Frame Press, The Dewdrop, and Cathexis Northwest Press. We’re doing pretty good if we can just get out alive is his first full-length poetry book. Vibrating with reverence and spirit of the Pacific Northwest, this collection of poems is a raw, lyrical eulogy for fated beloveds, sublime landscape, and ephemeral wonder that spans the vastness of time and place. Oyster-Sands showcases a true talent for imbuing the smallest human details with authenticity and layered meanings. Each poem maps out the human heart in relation to that larger human heart we all share together, in all their internal conflicts, with precision and grace. Adam Oyster-Sands is a high school Language Arts teacher and poet. We’re doing pretty good if we can just get out alive is his first full-length poetry book. Adam can often be found with his partner Morgan running through forests or walking their dogs around their neighborhood in Portland, Oregon. Scott Cannon draws, paints, writes poetry and short fiction, does woodworking, plays music, and publishes whatever he wants to with his friends. Arrive at 6:30 p.m. to grab a snack or drink. The event will start at 7:00 p.m. \\\\\* Event cohosted by BOLD Coffee & Books and Indigo: Editing, Design, and More.

events.summary: Let's kick-off the 'neighborhood trees' style planting season by planting in Central-South Vancouver neighborhoods! Interested in receiving a tree? Click HERE to purchase a tree for your household. Dozens of large \(6-10' tall\) trees will be ready for planting in their new homes, and your help is what makes this community planting possible! Please arrive by 8:45am to sign-in and be assigned a planting crew. The planting starts at 9:00am. We provide gloves, tools, and guidance, as well as light breakfast snacks and coffee/tea/hot chocolate. We ask that all volunteers dress for the weather, wear sturdy shoes/boots you don't mind getting dirty, and be ready to have fun! How do I register? Register by filling out this quick form . Groups, families, and individuals welcome! If your group is more than 5 people, please know you will be assigned to different planting crews. Want to plant by bike? Fill out this quick registration form . Bring your helmet and a bike trailer you're willing to move trees in, if you have one! Have a pickup truck? We need your help getting these young trees to their planting sites a few blocks away from the central staging site. Please sign up if you're able to help out in this key role. Under age 18? We request that youth 15 and under volunteer with a parent/guardian. Youth 16 and older can volunteer on their own and will need to hand us a youth waiver form signed by their parent/guardian. Private transportation: You will travel from the meeting location to a few planting sites in the nearby neighborhood \(up to several miles\). We recommend private transportation \(bike or vehicle\), but there may be an option to carpool if others in your small planting crew are also comfortable with this. Where will these trees be planted? In the following neighborhoods: Central Park, Columbia River, Dubois Park, Edgewood Park, Ellsworth Springs, Evergreen Highlands, Evergreen Shores, Forest Ridge, Harney Heights, Hudsons Bay, Marrion, North Garrison Heights, Northcrest, Northwood, Riverview, Southcliff, and Vancouver Heights. Questions? Please check out our Volunteer FAQ webpage . Our team is also happy to assist! Volunteer@friendsoftrees.org volunteer@friendsoftrees.org / 503-595-0213 We look forward to planting together soon! This event is in partnership with the City of Vancouver.
events.title: Central-South Vancouver neighborhood planting (Vancouver, WA)

events.summary: Vogue-published photographer Kenji Shimizu, Grammy-nominated producer and artist rei mastrogiovanni, and doctoral candidate in Japanese literature Teppei Fukuda together crafted this selection of photographs that portray Oregon’s four seasons through a critical reimagining of Japanese seasonal aesthetics. Drawing on the visual techniques of sumi-e ink painting, the five sets of photographs express seasonality through portraiture, gesture, everyday objects, and atmosphere. At the same time, the artists are exploring the relationship between tradition and cultural identity as Japanese and multi-heritage Japanese artists living in Oregon, superimposing one of the most prevalent motifs in Japanese art onto a new context. The individual artists’ works will also be on display, as well as artwork from the museum’s collection.

events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. Plan your visit and explore the exhibition: worldforestry.org/lookout-landscape
events.title: Lookout Landscape Exhibition

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Once upon a time in postwar Italy . . . Vittorio De Sica’s follow-up to his international triumph Bicycle Thieves is an enchanting neorealist fairy tale in which he combined his celebrated slice-of-life poetry with flights of graceful comedy and storybook fantasy. On the outskirts of Milan, a band of vagabonds work together to form a shantytown. When it is discovered that the land they occupy contains oil, however, it’s up to the cherubic orphan Totò (Francesco Golisano)—with some divine help—to save their community from greedy developers. Tipping their hats to the imaginative whimsy of Charles Chaplin and René Clair, De Sica and screenwriter Cesare Zavattini (adapting his own novel) craft a big-hearted ode to the nobility of everyday people
events.title: Miracle in Milan (1951)

As citizens invested in hope for a future built on love and care, we know that the next generation requires our attention to nourish them into becoming the compassionate, responsible, and thoughtful humans the next chapter of humanity needs. The works in this show feature images centering play, connection, and collaboration as enriching elements of young people's lives. The artists: Sasha Wilk, Gabe Wolfe, Kyra Watkins, Elizabeth Goss, Stefania Salles Bruins, Corinne Kenly Barber, Forest Salazar, Danny Stephens and Kristie Winther. events.summary: Come enjoy Leslie McMillan’s one-of-a-kind handcrafted jewelry and painter bd dombrowsky’s visual explorations of the mischievous silver night and the many insights the capricious muse offers. Painter bd dombrowsky My visual style is derived from an interest in vintage illustrated books -- encyclopedias, primers, comics, and stories-- all the simple visual devices we use as a culture to educate and socialize ourselves. Much of my work is informed by myths and folklore as I relate our old stories and weave them into new stories. Using my background in drama, sculpture and printmaking, my goal is to craft a resonant space in which these stories are allowed to unfold, drawn from our shared mythos but reimagined by me and narrated by the viewer themselves. Jewelry Artist Leslie McMillan As a jewelry smith I am all over the place. To begin with I have ADHD, so my mind is manic. I roam from fusing gold on steel to traditional silversmithing to bonding Japanese silver leaf. When working with steel and gold, I am drawn to the truth that you cannot control the outcome. By heating the gold high enough to fuse with the steel, it takes on a life of its own and travels where it wants to go. When approaching sterling silver and natural stones, I follow a more traditional method. Creating hand-forged settings and sourcing stones from First Nation lapidary artists are fundamental to my work. No matter the process, I rely on inspiration from the great Pacific Northwest and all its natural beauty to influence my final piece. October 29 through November 23, 11am-7pm Last Thursday Opening Reception, October 29, 6-9pm
events.title: Moonlight Mischief: Jewelry and Paintings

She is the author of The Taste of Home, Where The Heart Belongs 家的味道，心的归属, a bi-lingual cookbook that celebrates the emotional connections we build through food and a fundraising initiative that supports the pantry’s mission. Anna also leads the Asian Food Pantry program at the Community for Positive Aging \(Hollywood Senior Center\), where she supports low-income Asian seniors by providing culturally familiar foods and fostering community connection. A longtime volunteer at Lan Su Chinese Garden, Anna is deeply committed to promoting and preserving Chinese culture through her work and community engagement. events.summary: Discover the extraordinary and magical life of Eva Castellanoz: campesina, wife, mother, cultural guardian, artist, and curandera. After immigrating from Mexico, Eva worked the fields alongside her parents, but that was before she discovered her true calling—she was a crown maker. Through her heritage and artistry, she became a healer, binding the hearts of her community while surviving heartbreak of her own. Eva’s life was full of everyday magic—from her childhood in Texas to marriage and motherhood in Nyssa, Oregon, Eva created a life that is full of art, community, and healing. Portland Opera proudly presents this latest installment of the Our Oregon series, a collection of original youth operas that examines Oregon history by highlighting the lives of extraordinary Oregonian women through a variety of lenses.

events.summary: New Room Studios is proud to present this Portland debut show by the Genius Artist Fellow and matter painter Jeff Beers. “Paper & Raincoat” are the two main ingredients of a new series that unfolds like a myth cycle of life and death. Beers painstakingly made it out of scraps of thin sheets of paper that he’s aged for 30 years, and surplus raincoat material from Columbia Sportswear. \(Beers got the latter from the local nonprofit SCRAP Creative Reuse.\) After 16 months of meticulous work, these two simple ingredients have found cosmic depths in this series of 8 pieces. The show also includes a series of Beers’ earlier, more earthy and elemental works. These pieces use tars, paints, emulsions and waxes to explore simultaneously the microcosms and macrocosms of the materials. Rarely able to afford art supplies, Beers \(newrooms.org/artists/jeff-beers\) learned at an early age how to make his own. He still makes his own paints and emulsions, and his subject matter is often the materials that he’s foraged from the built environment and from the natural environment. He works with the materials until he learns their languages and how they want to see, and much of his art is in the discipline of letting them speak through him. Beers was awarded a 2025-2026 Genius Artist Fellowship by New Room Studios \(newrooms.org\). This program recognizes and supports artists who have a history of making excellent work over the years, despite significant barriers. As part of his Fellowship, New Room Studios is producing this show. This show is hosted by The Salmonberry Trail Foundation \(salmonberrytrail.org\), which is dedicated to building an 82-mile trail for hiking and biking from Banks to the Oregon Coast. “Jeff Beers: Paper & Raincoat” will take over their spacious and historic office in downtown Portland in November.
events.title: Jeff Beers: Paper & Raincoat

events.summary: This exhibition highlights a distinct artistic collaboration between printmakers Cassie Ferguson and Charlie Cohan, marking the creative intersection of their independent yet interrelated studios, Lost Bearings Press (LBP) and BurnPrint Studio (BPS). Centered on a shared dedication to traditional printmaking, the showcase features a diverse range of techniques, including stone lithography, screen printing, polyester plate lithography, and relief printmaking. The conceptual foundation of this exhibition hinges on a collaborative print created by Cohan and Ferguson in 2017, which juxtaposed the iconic Burnside Skatepark with an urban overpass. This visual conversation continues in Ferguson’s ongoing series of stone lithographs capturing DIY skateparks. Her work seeks to honor and archive the subcultural spaces that have shaped her lived experience. Because these grassroots spaces often thrive under overpasses and within neglected industrial zones, her prints seamlessly connect with Cohan’s imagery of Portland’s monumental bridges. Together, the artists offer a multifaceted view of the city, championing the gritty beauty of structural environments. Their works invite viewers to reflect on their own relationship to the municipal landscape and to find new ways of seeing everyday urban scenes. Additionally, the exhibition introduces recent work by Nakemiah “Kiki” Williams, produced in collaboration with Ferguson and Cohan at LBP and BPS. This project marks the debut publication for LBP and brings their history full circle, as both Williams and Ferguson are alumnae of Cohan’s printmaking program at the University of Hawai’i at Mānoa. This collaboration marks the beginning of collaborative print work at LBP, which is now open for publishing and contracted prints of primarily stone lithographs.
events.title: Under the Overpass

events.summary: BOLD is thrilled to host Demystifying Workplace Protections for Medical Leave and More: A Speaker Event Hosted by the Chronic Pain Project. This talk by Rosa Park Neves is designed to empower people with chronic illness and their families with clear, actionable knowledge regarding their employment rights. As a Paid Leave Strategist with a background in Human Resource (HR) Management (including Benefits Administration and Leave Management), Rosa can bridge the gap between complex policy and real-world application. Key Learning Objectives \-Individual Protections: Understanding workplace accommodations and job security for various chronic illness conditions. \-Support for Caregivers: Navigating family leave options for loved ones assisting through diagnosis and treatment. \-Inside Perspectives: Leveraging my experience as a former HR Generalist as well as Unemployment Claims Adjudicator to explain how leave and benefits are evaluated from a regulatory standpoint. The Goal To bridge the gap between dense legislative language and the reality of a living with chronic illness. We aim to clarify workplace protections for both patients and their loved ones, ensuring that professional stability remains intact during the most challenging moments of treatment. Rosa Park Neves of RP7 Online LLC is a Paid Leave Strategist specializing in the intersection of health and the workplace. With a degree in Human Resource Management and experience in benefits administration, they bring a deep understanding of general corporate, state and federal policies. Furthermore, their previous role as a state-contracted Unemployment Claims Adjudicator provides a rare, "inside-out" view of how leave protections are enforced. Last but not least, on a personal note Rosa is a working mom with multiple chronic illnesses raising 2 children in a bi-lingual, multi-generational, neurodiverse household RSVP is preferred and registration is limited. Tickets are pay-what-you-can with a suggested price of $15/General Admission and $30/Pay It Forward. Registration is available here: https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/demystifying-workplace-protections-for-medical-leave-and-more

events.summary: Selected chants from Tudor England Tudor England (c1485–1603) was deeply unstable—yet monuments of its Latin sacred music survived, including the Sarum rite chant used before the Reformation. This chant formed the basis of devotional works by Taverner, Sheppard, Fayrfax, and Tye. It appears directly in several pieces on this program—among them Sheppard’s deeply moving Libera nos, whose chant melody is shown here. This music is inseparable too from the stone abbeys and cathedrals it was made to fill. These Stones Remain restores these masterworks to their spiritual home, performed by the Northwest’s own Tudor Choir.
events.title: These Stones Remain

events.summary: Portland Mezzo-Soprano & Composer Dr. Lisa Neher launches Pacific Art Song (pacificartsong.com), a concert series dedicated to Western Classical Art Song, with a program titled Summer Nights. A celebration of French song, the program transports audiences to the era of intimate salons, where friends gathered in living rooms to enjoy music shared up close. The centerpiece of the program, Hector Berlioz’s Les Nuits d'été (Summer Nights), explores longing, loss, and love across five songs that set vibrant poetry with closely interwoven parts for the voice and the piano. The work is the first major song cycle written by a French composer. Complimenting Berlioz’s groundbreaking piece are masterworks by Pauline Viardot and protégé Lili Boulanger, brilliant French women composers long marginalized due to their gender.Completing the program are two world premieres composed by Neher herself. Chanson d’automne (Song of Autumn) and L’heure du berger (The Hour of the Shepherd) set poetry of Paul Verlaine. Dubbed “Prince of Poets” by his peers, Verlaine’s name is synonymous with French song. Why art song now? “We’re living in an era of 15 second Tiktok videos and the constant dopamine rush of notifications on our devices,” says Neher. “But what we’re all longing for is something real and embodied. This concert is an invitation to slow down and connect with your senses, to hear and see and feel the music in a community.” PERFORMERS Dr. Lisa Neher, mezzo-soprano & composer Hannah Early, piano Susan McBerry, guest lecturer There will be a pre-concert talk by Susan McBerry at 2:40 pm.
events.title: Pacific Art Song: Summer Nights

events.summary: Lloyd Jones is a consummate guitarist/singer/songwriter/arranger/performer/ bandleader. One of the most original artists on the modern day blues scene, Jones is, in the words of Blues Revue, "certainly worthy of greater recognition." The release of his first recording for Blind Pig Records, Love Gotcha, should bring him the national and international acclamation he deserves. Jones was born in Seattle into a musical family, which moved to Portland soon afterward. "I remember music was everywhere in our house growing up. My dad was playing Dixieland jazz records and trying to teach me to play trumpet when I was only five years old. My older brother played drums and showed me how. Then he took me to his band rehearsals and had me playing gigs when I was just 13. He took me to see James Brown in '64. You've got to imagine James in '64 - ouch! Then B.B. King, Buddy Guy, even Sonny Terry and Brownie McGhee - all this before I was out of high school. I was underage and totally mesmerized" Jones got deep into the blues and was the leader of Portland's most popular blues bands, Brown Sugar, in the early 70's. "We got to work with touring musicians in those days, like Charlie Musselwhite, George "Harmonica" Smith, the Johnny Otis show, Big Mama Thornton and Big Walter Horton. That's how we learned, and that's really when I first picked up the guitar. A lot of times these people would stay at our homes and teach us music and history. Some of them have passed now, so I cherish those memories. S.P. Leary, who was in Muddy Waters band and was playing drums with Big Walter at the time, leaned over to me as he was leaving town and said, "Man, I'm getting old. You gotta keep it alive. It's a struggle sometimes, but if you love it, you keep on struggling."' Through the years Jones would continue to hone his craft by performing with the likes of Albert Collins, Robert Cray, Bonnie Raitt, Taj Mahal, B.B. King, Dr. John, John Hammond, Etta James, Junior Wells and Buddy Guy, and many more music legends. In the 80's Jones joined forces with ex-Robert Cray singer/harp player Curtis Salgado in a band called In Yo' Face. "That was one fun band! Seemed like we all had the same record collection. Curtis really pushed me as a guitar player, and when he left in '85 to join Roomful of Blues I knew it was time to play my music." Jones knew what he wanted to say and how he wanted to say it. The Lloyd Jones Struggle started in 1985 as a vehicle for his songwriting. "I love a good story. Most of the traditional blues stayed with a shuffle or slow blues. Being a drummer I keep hearing the rhythm of the words all broke down funky and swamp-afied; nice and relaxed but kind of turned inside out." Jones made two recordings in the late 80's for Criminal Records: The Lloyd Jones Struggle \(1987\) and Small Potatoes \(1989\). They won over a dozen local music awards, as well as acclaim from national music publications such as Down Beat and Guitar Player, which in turn led to some extensive touring for the band on the Miller Beer Sponsorship Program. In 1993 Jones released his third album, Lloyd \`Have Mercy' Jones - Live! on the Burnside Records label. In 1995 Lloyd Jones recorded a highly acclaimed album for the Audio Quest label, entitled Trouble Monkey. Blues Revue named it, "not only one of the best albums of 1995, it is one of the best albums of the 1990's," while Robert Cray called it "the best damn record I've heard in a long time!" Vintage Guitar Magazine said, "Jones offers vocals that would make Sam and Dave smile and guitar work Steve Cropper would be proud of" and referred to his affecting vocals as "gritty as a dirt road and smooth as melting butter." Lloyd's songwriting was starting to be noticed as well, with Joe Louis Walker and Gatemouth Brown covering two of his compositions. Jones and his band have become a mainstay on the West Coast circuit, and have brought their tasteful, crowd-pleasing brand of music from New Orleans to Canada to the Caribbean, where Delbert McClinton witnessed a performance and remarked, "When I heard Lloyd Jones live for the first time in January 1999, it was like exhaling after holding my breath for fifteen years." It was such a typically memorable set at the Santa Cruz Blues Festival that led to Jones' signing by Blind Pig Records. Jones describes his soulful and intelligent fusion of funk, blues, and R&B as "storytelling with a Memphis groove." His latest CD, Love Gotcha, presents Lloyd's writing at its trenchant best. His songs have the quality that makes them sound as if they have been around as blues standards for years or they seem to have fallen out of some time warp from the golden days of R&B. His approach to the guitar is both economical and rhythmically sophisticated, with a style that can be as delicate as it is devastating. And Jones' accomplished guitar and vocal work are complemented throughout the recording by some of the funkiest horn-rhythm-organ arrangements around. Blues lovers everywhere are about to discover what Lloyd Jones' fans already know - one taste of his beguiling music and you're captivated. Lloyd's gotcha! Blind Pig Records A division of Whole Hog, Inc. PO. Box 2344, San Francisco, CA 94126

From there, the intensity gradually rises into a strong, athletic Power Vinyasa practice. Expect creative sequencing, dynamic flows, and building heat as you cultivate strength, mobility, presence, and full-body energy. The class will wind down with dance before settling into a deeply restorative, long savasana. This final stillness allows your nervous system to integrate the effort, movement, and joy of the practice. No dance experience required - come move, breathe, and have fun. All levels welcome.
events.title: Flow State: EDM Power Vinyasa with Alexie + Karen

events.summary: The Bylines are a Portland based band created by Reece Marshburn and Marianna Thielen who write and perform sophisticated, jazz-inspired, story-driven pop music. They tour the Northwest regularly as a duo, and put on theatrical shows with their full ensemble. They are alumni of the Johnny Mercer Songwriters Project and have played before Randy Newman. Portland's The Bylines exists in a unique musical plane, one at once grounded in the big-band past of glamorous pop performances and rooted in a present realm of intricate and highly addictive songwriting. With a focus on grand live spectacle--a facet of music often lost in the digital age--the group is equally at home in velvet-curtained jazz halls, large rooms and intimate venues. That sound is the product of a marriage both sonic and literal. The Bylines is made up of two songwriters whose styles and influences converge to bring The Bylines' catchy, addictive sounds to vibrant life. Frontwoman Marianna Thielen, the glamorous face of the group, brings to the fore a background in composition, classical vocal work and, most obviously, musical theater, illuminating the stage with endlessly watchable bravado backed up by her powerful -- yet playful -- vocal prowess. Meanwhile, gliding his fingers across the keys is Reece Marshburn, letting loose a symphony of intricate melodies rooted in a combination of classical, jazz and pop music. The resulting combination is a unique pop confection drawing on decades of influences, as if Cole Porter, Carole King, Dusty Springfield, Freddie Mercury, Paul Simon, Rufus Wainwright and Regina Spektor combined forces and filtered their unique compositions through classical maestros and film composers, then sprinkled it with a keen pop sensibility and a commitment to putting on the most involving, charismatic and personalized live shows this side of the Copacabana. The Bylines have used their unique-yet-familiar sound to play to audiences large and small throughout the country, and have released both a studio\(self titled, recorded by Bob Stark at Kung Fu Bakery\) and a live album\(The Bylines Live, recorded at the Alberta Rose Theatre in Portland, OR\). The Bylines are proud alumni of the Johnny Mercer Songwriting Project, and have had support from the Regional Arts and Culture Council. Whether performing as a Thielen/Marshburn duo or with a larger band, the result is a blend of butter-smooth melodies, densely layered songwriting and powerful vocals. Most importantly, though, The Bylines musical cocktail goes down easy, and emphasizes something that is so often forgotten when such prolific songwriters present their craft: listening to music is, above all, supposed to be an experience… and a fun one.
events.title: The Bylines

events.summary: The Goddamn Gallows Spit from the heart of America's Rust Belt, arising from a night of flophouse violence. Drifting across the states, they cemented their sound in Portland, OR and later in Los Angeles, CA, where they lived in abandoned buildings, squatter camps, storage units and shoebox apartments. In 2007, they left everything behind and spent the next 4 years living out of whatever vehicle would get them to the next town. Building upon their original sound of twanged-out, punk rock gutterbilly \(Life of Sin 2004 and Gutterbillyblues 2007\), they began picking up stray musicians along the way and adding to their sound; washboard, accordion, mandolin and banjo \(Ghost of the Rails 2009 and 7 Devils 2011\) creating a sound referred to as "hobocore", "gypsy-punk" or "americana-punk", while never being stuck in any one sound. Enter 2018 and The Goddamn Gallows have reinvented themselves once again with The Trial. From rockabilly, psychobilly and punk rock, to bluegrass and metal, The Trial infuses disparate sounds into a new strange recipe of seamless genre bending profundities. Chock full of impromptu antics of the shocking variety and hauntingly eclectic instrumentation, The Goddamn Gallows have made legions of fans with their legendary, live shows.
events.title: The Goddamn Gallows

ON SCREEN: Unzipped 1995. Directed by Douglas Keeve. Runtime: 1 hour 16 minutes. Designer Isaac Mizrahi proved a force of nature on the road to his legendary fall 1994 collection, a career-defining triumph that was documented with an effervescent intimacy by Douglas Keeve, Mizrahi's then-partner. Both a time capsule of the buoyant, raucous 1990s, when pop culture and high art became interchangeable, and a vérité-style, in-the-trenches report on the daily agonies and ecstasies of the creative process, this seminal artistic portrait-sumptuously shot by Ellen Kuras and Robert Leacock-transcends glitz and glamour to offer an extraordinary view of the charisma and force of will inherent to genius, as well as its personal costs. This 4K film has been digitally restored by the Sundance Institute and UCLA Film & Television Archive. "A joy!"- Vogue "The perfect film." -Lena Dunham "You have to see this documentary!" - Charli XCX "Among the greatest fashion documentaries of all time." - Vanity Fair UNORTHODOX DOCS

events.summary: The third full-length from Margaret Glaspy, Echo The Diamond emerged from a deliberate stripping-away of artifice to reveal life for all its harsh truths and ineffable beauty. “This record came from trying to meet life on life’s terms, instead of looking for a happy ending in everything,” says the New York-based musician. “The whole experience of creating it felt like effortless catharsis.” Produced by Glaspy with co-production from her partner, Julian Lage, Echo The Diamond expands on the frenetic vitality of her 2016 release Emotions and Math. She was joined in the studio by drummer/percussionist David King \(The Bad Plus\) and bassist Chris Morrissey. Anchored in the raw yet mesmerizing vocal presence and impressionistic guitar work she’s brought to the stage in touring with the likes of Spoon and Wilco, Echo The Diamond holds entirely true to the spirit of its lyrical explorations, presenting a selection of songs both unvarnished and revelatory.

events.summary: From bayou kitchens to front porches, this captivating play celebrates the heart, humor, and resilience of Louisiana's women. Pull up a chair and savor a celebration of the remarkable women whose strength and spirit have always been the secret ingredient in Louisiana’s gumbo. This show is for you if you’ve ever wondered… Where do I belong? Where is home? What is a Cajun? What’s a Creole? Are they more than just styles of cooking? How different are Southerners from Northwesterners? How do you make a roux? What’s Mardi Gras all about anyway? What’s the deal with New Orleans and voodoo, vampires, and above ground graves? How do you “laissez les bon temps rouler”? Can you be both proud and ashamed of where you come from? How do you pronounce geaux, lagniappe, Ouachita, Tchoupitoulas, or couillon? Do you know what it means to miss New Orleans? Shelley Tate's one-woman show developed as an ensemble piece: a 90-minute show about history and culture of Louisiana —served with heart, humor, and just the right amount of spice. The gumbo is rich, the laughter is loud, and the women are unforgettable. GUMBO "...a steel magnolia in the Rose City" Performs Fridays & Saturdays at 7:30pm and Sunday at 2:00pm, November 6-15th, 2026. Tickets $15 at Magentatheater.com.
events.title: GUMBO by Shelley Tate at Magenta Theater

events.summary: At a time when many theatres are closing their doors or reducing programming, 100 Lives Repertory in Portland’s Buckman neighborhood is celebrating the inaugural season in its brand-new space. And the first play is a doozy: a sleek, sly, sci-fi mystery titled Anthropology, penned by Lauren Gunderson, one of America’s most produced playwrights. Anthropology is about a grieving computer coder, Merril, who builds an AI replica of her missing and presumed dead sister. Adding to the loss, Merril’s relationship with her girlfriend has come to an end, which draws her deeper and deeper into her ‘project’ of bringing back a version of her sister, to help heal her grief and lessen her loneliness. This is the Oregon premiere of Anthropology which had its world debut in London at Hampstead Theatre in 2023. The play runs Thursday through Sunday from October 23 through November 15. events.summary: Elanor Moss grew up in a very creative, devoutly Catholic family, and began playing music at church events. Homeschooled through early youth, her parents put a real emphasis on nature, reading and music. Eventually leaving the faith, Moss started writing songs of her own in York as a student of English literature and playing open mics around the city. While at University she also discovered songwriting greats: Leonard Cohen, Joni Mitchell, Bob Dylan, The Beatles. Shortly after graduation, Moss met producer Oli Deakin, who offered to record her first EP, “Citrus." Her work with Deakin took her to New York City, where she began forging a sense of community. Between “Citrus” and her second EP, “Cosmic,” Moss toured with Christian Lee Hutson, Benjamin Francis Leftwich, and LYR, played one-off shows with Cassandra Jenkins, CMAT, and Sam Amidon, and performed at Pitchfork London, Green Man Festival, and Mosely Folk, among others.

Classic soul meets rock-and-roll swagger. The Wooden Chicken has been a roadhouse institution on NE Sandy since 1978. Our community of customers is built upon the local residents and businesses that patronize our pub. Whether it be a Sunday 49er game, a softball team post-game function, or a get-together after a round of golf, all are welcome in our doors. Known famously for our fish and chips, our menu centers on classic bar food, cold beer, and classic cocktails. There are two origin stories that our patrons like to whisper: Originally farmland, the lot at NE 125th and Sandy, unearthed petrified chicken corpses during the development of the property, and hence the name of our beloved tavern, The Wooden Chicken Pub, was born. The second account is that a group was standing around in the parking lot, trying to figure out what to name the pub. All they could see was piles of lumber and empty buckets of KFC on the ground. Hence, “The Wooden Chicken.” Whichever story you prefer, we hope to see you soon.

events.summary: Big love to Shwayze for inviting me to celebrate a special chapter in our collective lives at McMenamin's in Portland. I typically remark how our generation lucked out growing up without the internet, only to be given it during such curious years - ultimately using it to download mixtapes off Dat Piff and share our discoveries with friends. I’m fortunate to have found myself in the scrapbook of many people’s fondest years. Having made music connected to several firsts, it played a part in experiences that a story could never truly do justice. There’s a certain joy we share having grown up at a similar time, maintaining an unspoken understanding because we were there, together, free of consequence and full of delusion. Let’s celebrate that. Catch you soon, my friends!
