events.summary: “Simulation Theory” posits that reality and existence as we know them to be are merely a computer simulation. Of course, The Matrix explored such a possibility in 1999, while Elon Musk espouses this hypothesis as gospel for 2019. Regardless of the theory’s truth, humanity still thrives under the weight of all-encompassing technology and daily cyber advancements. Born Of Osiris preserve such humanity within a torrent of destructive polyrhythmic riffing, chaotic vocal transmissions, and synth disarray. The Chicago quintet—Ronnie Canizaro \[lead vocals\], Joe Buras \[keys, synthesizers, vocals\], Lee McKinney \[guitar\], Nick Rossi \[bass\], and Cameron Losch \[drums\]—perfect that approach on 2019’s aptly titled, The Simulation \[Sumerian Records\]. “When you listen to the record, I hope you investigate where you see yourself and the future going in terms of technology and artificial intelligence,” exclaims Buras. The musicians architected a beacon to transmit such a message since their 2007 emergence. Not only have they performed on stages with Judas Priest, Rob Zombie, Bring Me The Horizon, and more, but they also landed four consecutive entries on the Billboard Top 200, including A Higher Place \[2009\], The Discovery \[2011\], Tomorrow We Die Alive \[2013\], and Soul Sphere \[2015\]. Additionally, they garnered features from Guitar World, Brave Words, Metalsucks, and MetalInjection, to name a few. By looking back, the group made a major leap forward. They spent 2017 performing their breakthrough 2007 debut, The New Reign, in its entirety on the road. By the time the guys hit the studio with Nick Sampson \[Asking Alexandria, Of Mice & Men\] who produced vocals while McKinney produced and engineered the entire record instrumentally, the vision crystallized for their next evolution. “We usually don’t wait this long between records,” Buras continues. “By playing The New Reign, we got back to the original vibes. Once we really started writing, it was a combination of our old and new songwriting styles. The last three albums felt like a trilogy. On this one, we take the next step throughout putting all of our skills into one distinct body of work.” That included welcoming Rossi into the fold following the departure of original bassist David Da Rocha. Beyond the creative core of McKinney and Losch handling most of the writing, Rossi lent his writing talents to the process on a handful of songs. The music further incorporated instrumental virtuosity as well as entrancing synths and twin vocals. At the same time, Buras dove into books like Jacek Dukaj’s Perfect Imperfection, kickstarting a thematic thread. On the first single “The Accursed,” screeching keys entwine with precise and pummeling riffing before spiraling towards a hard-hitting and head-nodding groove. “The songs are more anthemic,” Buras says. “They’re about not giving up when things get difficult, you feel down, or a relationship isn’t working. Instead, you don’t stop and force on. We came into this lifestyle aware of the sacrifices. This is how we’re going to live it.” “Under The Gun” upholds that sentiment, while “Silence The Echo” steamrolls forward amidst a flurry airtight guitars and a percussive maelstrom. “That one dives into silencing negative thoughts,” he elaborates. “We all feel down sometimes, but you silence those thoughts and keep moving.” In the end—whether a simulation or not—Born Of Osiris confidently embrace the future with open arms and deliver their boldest output yet. “There’s the technological side to the music, but there’s also a message of being patient and persevering,” he leaves off. “We’ve redefined our sound on this one. Everything is coming together. We’re brothers in this. It’s a new chapter for Born Of Osiris.”

events.summary: Alison’s Halo was formed in Tempe, Arizona during the fall of 1992 by Catherine Cooper \(Vocals/Guitar\), Adam Cooper \(Guitar\), David Rogers \(Bass/vocals\) and Roger Brogan \(Drums/Percussion\). Within months of formation the band burst onto the local scene and immediately began securing shows with national acts \(The Verve, Ultra Vivid Scene, Curve, The Boo Radleys, Stereophonics, Medicine, Lovesliescrushing, Bailter Space and many others\) as well as being invited to perform at numerous music festivals around the country. The Dozen/Calendar single was released by the legendary Independent Project Records in 1995 to wonderful national reviews and extensive college radio airplay. The single’s beautiful blend of chiming guitar noise and Catherine’s breathtaking melodies perked many an ear and led to the band loading up the van and heading out for a successful string of tour dates around the country. Their debut full-length, Eyedazzler, was recorded to various 2, 4, & 8 porta-studio cassettes from 1992-1996 and released on Detroit’s Burnt Hair Records in 1998. This stunning collection of songs has only grown in popularity since its original release and has been ranked among the top shoegaze and dreampop records from the golden eras of both genres.

events.summary: Apukuna is a visionary DJ and musician whose musical offerings transcend the ordinary, creating powerful, heart-centered journeys that ignite dance floors, guide ambient sound journeys, and deepen breathwork sessions. His distinctive approach to DJ'ing relies on looping, live remixing, live vocals, and digital percussion to craft unique and improvised experiences. Known for his ability to blend sacred music with soul-shaking movement, Apukuna's journeys help to heal, uplift, and guide transformational experiences. He describes his creations as a ‘movement, a meditation, and a prayer for an awakening heart’. Apukuna is also singer-songwriter Jon David \(@jondavidmusic\) and an adept presenter and workshop facilitator, delving into the realms of conscious communication, community-building, and food. Apukuna has facilitated dance floors and workshops at BOOM Festival \(Portugal\), Dreamersland \(Poland\), Ecstatic Dance Festival \(Cyprus\), Beyond Music & Arts Festival \(Turkey\), Sonic Springs \(Canada\), Wicked Woods \(Canada\), Shambhala Music Festival \(Canada\), Lucidity Festival \(USA\), Lightning in a Bottle \(USA\), and Burning Man \(USA\). www.apukunamusic.com

events.summary: Carving her way through adolescence with a fierce artistic drive, Minneapolis-based musician Mother Soki discovered her passion for making music while attending college in Chicago. Immersed in everything she loves, she gravitated toward the dreamy textures of Dreampop and the sonic nostalgia of the ’90s. Drawing daily inspiration from her surroundings, she channels her creativity through classic influences: The Sundays, Imogen Heap, and Cocteau Twins. Her sound blends modern interpretations of vintage synths with heavy guitars and airy, spacious vocals—creating contrasts that shouldn't work, but somehow do. Mother Soki makes the unexpected feel seamless.

events.summary: Ben Caplan has always defied easy categorization. With his deep, commanding baritone and electrifying stage presence, he merges the raw energy of diverse folk traditions with modern innovation. His music isn’t just performed; it’s experienced. Now, with The Flood, Caplan takes his artistry to new depths, crafting an album that meditates on endings, resilience, and the art of carrying wisdom forward. Scheduled for release in May 2025, The Flood is both timely and timeless. “The world is ending for someone all the time,” Caplan muses. “But endings aren’t absolute. Cultures, ecosystems, civilizations—they evolve, adapt. This album is about finding the pieces that survive and carrying them forward.” Musically, The Flood is a collision of past and future. Melodically tilted towards the folk traditions of Eastern Europe, the album reinvents these sounds with timeless lyrics and modern production. Clarinet melodies soar over pulsing synthesizers; grand pianos give way to sequenced rhythms. The result is an intricate sonic tapestry—both ancient and urgent. With nearly 2,000 performances across 27 countries, Caplan’s live shows are known for their raw energy and emotional depth. The Flood is designed with the stage in mind—its seamless transitions and dynamic arrangements promise an immersive concert experience. “Music holds space for people. My hope is that this project allows listeners to confront the grief of endings, but also find joy in what’s ahead.”
events.title: Yaelokre & Ben Caplan & Keath Ósk

events.summary: TICKETS: truewest.info/Hazard26 Tickets On Sale Friday, June 12th at 10am PT This Event is 21\+ ---------------------------------------- The story of Waterville, OH indie-folk trio Oliver Hazard - Michael Belazis \(vocals, guitar\) and Devin East \(vocals, guitar\), joined by Nate Miner \(keys, vocals\)–is a modern take on classic band mythmaking. One member returned home to Ohio after leading camping trips in California and decided to make an album with two childhood friends. They won a Facebook raffle to record one song at a studio–but instead, they played their entire album straight through in a single take, resulting in their 2018 debut LP, 34 N River. The album was hailed as a “folk-pop masterpiece” by The Fader, and soon after, the band landed slots at Bonnaroo and Mountain Jam. In 2019, they released their 6-track EP, The Flood, which Billboard described as a “souvenir.” Their self-titled sophomore album followed in July 2023, incorporating music from their earlier Northern Lights EP along with five new songs. Most recently, they released their Raindrop River EP in December 2024. Oliver Hazard’s next chapter continues to tell the story of Waterville, Ohio–a small town with a big heart. Their music serves as a soundtrack to everyday life, lifting spirits and inviting listeners to find beauty in the ordinary.
events.title: Oliver Hazard

This work helps to increase Pacific Northwest ecosystem diversity in an expanding habitat area and supports our collaborative Back 5 educational project. No experience necessary! The Leach Botanical Garden is a hidden gem in outer SE Portland. Beyond the manicured paths of the garden are several acres of forests and fields which have become overrun by Himalayan blackberry, English ivy, and other plants that discourage diversity. The garden needs your help to become a healthy ecosystem again! Thank you for volunteering to join us in opening spaces to promote a healthy ecosystem in the Leach Botanical Garden! Volunteers are encouraged to enjoy the rest of the garden after the event. Click Here to RSVP Questions? Email sara@jcwc.org What: land tending, trail maintenance, and weeding. When: Wednesday, December 9th, 2026, 9am-12pm Where: Leach Botanical Garden \(see directions below\) What to bring: Bring a filled water bottle and snacks. You’re welcome to bring gloves and tools, if you want to use your own. What to wear: Dress for the weather! Wear long thick pants, a long-sleeved shirt, and sturdy shoes for uneven terrain that you don’t mind getting muddy. Bring a raincoat or a hat and sunscreen, as appropriate. events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. events.summary: This former Southern Pacific Railroad station, fondly called the Old Train Station \(OTS\), is home to Friends of Historic Forest Grove. The Old Train Station now serves as a museum highlighting about 150 years of local history, from photographs and maps to clothing and furniture. It also houses an historic library and research center. Built in 1913, the station handled passenger and light freight service into 1929. After that only light freight came through. Burlingham and Sons purchased the building as office space for their seed company. Unfortunately, over the years this building has gone through some internal and external changes but some of the original station remains and can easy be found. Woodfold acquired the building from Burlingham and has graciously allowed Friends to use the building since 2008. Please stop by and see what we have to offer. Check website to confirm open hours
events.title: Friends of Historic Forest Grove Museum & Library Open

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Ripe remembers sweating to hell in a basement underneath a Subway sandwich shop, buildingtheir very first songs in a concrete cube that smelled like fresh bread. They remember sellingtheir first tickets by hand outside the coffee shop that their friends worked at, holding court liketwenty-something impresarios trying to move like 50 tickets to a bar that was willing to let youkeep the ticket sales if they kept the bar. In a world where we constantly feel the loving pressure to "tell our story", where so many of ourfriends that have found success as artists have done it alone, Ripe is using their bio to tell youthat at the center of everything is collaboration and community, a friendship that has become abond as strong as family, a constantly spinning object that cannot be properly captured by anysingle still photograph. This moment, the two songs already out and the new songs coming, catches the band in amoment of intense joyous swelling energy. Working in dream studios, in a city they spent yearstrying to take a proper chance on, with a producer that had made albums we loved in ourformative years, alongside the closest musical relations we've formed. This is our love letter tocomplicated nostalgia, to relentless empowering change, to realizing that making dreams cometrue (just like a crisis) only fully makes sense when it is shared. Joy in the wild unknown let us tell you who we were. Bright blues had us ripped apart so wecould start again. What comes next is the band swinging for the fences, all in at the table,risking everything for a shot at feeling connected to you. Thank you for being here.
events.title: RIPE

events.summary: Vogue-published photographer Kenji Shimizu, Grammy-nominated producer and artist rei mastrogiovanni, and doctoral candidate in Japanese literature Teppei Fukuda together crafted this selection of photographs that portray Oregon’s four seasons through a critical reimagining of Japanese seasonal aesthetics. Drawing on the visual techniques of sumi-e ink painting, the five sets of photographs express seasonality through portraiture, gesture, everyday objects, and atmosphere. At the same time, the artists are exploring the relationship between tradition and cultural identity as Japanese and multi-heritage Japanese artists living in Oregon, superimposing one of the most prevalent motifs in Japanese art onto a new context. The individual artists’ works will also be on display, as well as artwork from the museum’s collection.

events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. Plan your visit and explore the exhibition: worldforestry.org/lookout-landscape
events.title: Lookout Landscape Exhibition

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: The spirited California-based five piece has waved a blindingly brilliant hardcore torch for over 25 years. Their aggressive yet melodic brand of music is catchy, well written, and timeless enough to seep into your brain, your blood, and your heart; these songs will stay with you forever. In today’s overpopulated music scene, standing out and making yourself memorable are essential survival tools. Ignite have mastered the art of memorable melodies without sacrificing an ounce of intensity, aggression, or heart. They’ve got a proven, rabid fan-base that populates over 50 countries. People go crazy for Ignite all over the world, including Europe, Australia, South America, Canada and in their native US, and that’s why the band lives on the road, bringing the fans what they want and what they need. Ignite has released six albums and one live dvd/cd: IGNITE S/T \(2022\) A War Against You \(2016\), Our Darkest Days Live \(2012\), Our Darkest Days \(2006\), A Place Called Home \(2000\), Past Our Means \(1996\) and Call On My Brothers \(1995\), all of which enjoy a place in the hardcore canon.

THE EXPERIENCE Join Lesbian Cinema Club for Barbara Forever-an archive-driven exploration of the life, work, and legacy of iconic, pioneering lesbian filmmaker Barbara Hammer. A special zine and merch will be on sale in advance of the screening. ON SCREEN: Barbara Forever \+ Love, Barbara Love, Barbara. 2022. Directed by Brydie O'Connor. Runtime 15min. Not Rated. A touching tribute to the pioneering lesbian experimental filmmaker, Barbara Hammer, told through the lens and love of her partner of over 30 years. Barbara Forever. 2026. Directed by Brydie O'Connor. Runtime 1hr 42min. Not Rated. Barbara Forever explores the films, archive, and ongoing cultural impact of experimental filmmaker Barbara Hammer, revealing her ingenious lifelong artistic effort to create and record lesbian histories, personal and societal. Through her own images and words, the film centers Hammer as a prism of the cultural ecosystems around her through the feminist and queer movements in 1970s San Francisco, the male-dominated New York art world of the 1980s, the New Queer Cinema movement of the 1990s, and expanded LGBTQIA\+ representation in art and culture in the 2000s. ON STAGE: Lesbian Cinema Club Lesbian Cinema Club is a Portland local screening series and gathering that started in the summer of 2025 as a top surgery fundraiser for lead organizer and programmer, Noname. The series started in a backyard with a few friends with a simple goal to watch and learn about Lesbian artists and filmmakers while fundraising for gender affirming care. The series quickly became a large community gathering for local queer and lesbian film-lovers. QUEER CINE

events.summary: Your favorite local public radio show Live Wire is bringing its season finale to Revolution Hall on Thursday, December 10th! Host Luke Burbank will be joined by drag queen and environmental activist Pattie Gonia, comedian and podcast host Ophira Eisenberg, and pioneering queercore punk band Team Dresch. Show starts at 7:30pm. Doors open at 6:30pm. Live Wire Members receive 15% off. To get tickets, visit www.livewireradio.org/live-shows/20261210! ABOUT THE GUESTS Pattie Gonia is an environmentalist, drag queen, and community organizer. They've been named to the TIME100 list, honored as Outside Magazine's Person of the Year, and included on National Geographic's 33 list. They have also raised more than $3 million for grassroots BIPOC and Queer non-profits and co-founded the Outdoorist Oath, a nonprofit that creates community and opportunities for allies, BIPOC, Queer and underrepresented groups to get outdoors. They're currently touring the country as the star of SAVE HER!, a drag show about the climate, politics, and the power of nature. Ophira Eisenberg is a comedian, writer, and podcast host who headlines theaters and comedy venues across the world, tours regularly with The Moth Mainstage, and hosts the weekly parenting-comedy podcast Parenting is a Joke. Her new comedy special I Used to Be Nicer is streaming now. She also hosted NPR’s trivia comedy show Ask Me Another for 9 years. Her breakout memoir Screw Everyone: Sleeping My Way to Monogamy has been optioned for a television series. Team Dresch are a legendary Portland-based punk band and a founding voice of the queercore movement. Formed in 1993, their albums Personal Best (1995) and Captain My Captain (1996) became touchstones of '90s queer punk. Furthermore, their third album and first album in 30 years is out this fall. And they remain legendary because, more than three decades later, they’re still going strong.
events.title: Luke Burbank w/ Pattie Gonia

events.summary: Vogue-published photographer Kenji Shimizu, Grammy-nominated producer and artist rei mastrogiovanni, and doctoral candidate in Japanese literature Teppei Fukuda together crafted this selection of photographs that portray Oregon’s four seasons through a critical reimagining of Japanese seasonal aesthetics. Drawing on the visual techniques of sumi-e ink painting, the five sets of photographs express seasonality through portraiture, gesture, everyday objects, and atmosphere. At the same time, the artists are exploring the relationship between tradition and cultural identity as Japanese and multi-heritage Japanese artists living in Oregon, superimposing one of the most prevalent motifs in Japanese art onto a new context. The individual artists’ works will also be on display, as well as artwork from the museum’s collection.
events.title: refractiv Photography Exhibition

events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. Plan your visit and explore the exhibition: worldforestry.org/lookout-landscape
events.title: Lookout Landscape Exhibition

This unforgettable exhibition includes site-specific installations and a hands-on touch wall that will make you rethink your relationship to cloth.
events.title: Weaving Time: NUNO – Textiles of Tradition and Transformation

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: What makes a movie magical? How did filmmakers create incredible illusions more than 100 years ago? And why does music make us feel so much more? Discover the extraordinary imagination of filmmaker Georges Méliès through film excerpts, explore the origins of cinematic special effects, and experiment with the tricks, sounds and musical ideas that can transform a moving image into a live experience. Join Jean-François Alcoléa, Artistic Director of Alcoléa & Cie and creator of Right in the Eye, for a playful behind-the-scenes journey into the world of early cinema and the creative process behind his live film-concert. In February 2027, you’ll have an opportunity to see this live film-concert presented at Portland Art Museum’s Whitsell Auditorium. Come curious, leave inspired, and discover how a little movie magic is made! Click here to visit Jean-François' website and learn more about his work. Watch the video below to get a glimpse into February's upcoming performance of Right in the Eye at the Whitsell Auditorium.

events.summary: Lucy Clearwater is a Los Angeles–based folk/Americana singer-songwriter who writes songs the way some people keep journals. Honestly, carefully, and with a deep respect for feeling. With a background in classical violin and a sound rooted in acoustic instruments and human-scale storytelling, her music carries emotional clarity, wit, and the warmth of California folk traditions. A 2024 Kerrville Folk Festival New Folk Competition winner, Clearwater has spent the last several years on the road, touring across the U.S., Canada, the U.K., and Europe. She's often seen sharing stages with her friends and fellow artists such as John Craigie, Ocie Elliott, Tyler Ballgame, Victoria Canal, Ye Vagabonds, Joe Pug, Martin Luke Brown, Luca Fogale, and others. Her debut album, People ≠ Possessions, arrived May 14, 2026, produced by Grammy-winner Tyler Chester and recorded mostly live to tape at Bell Choir Studios in Los Angeles. Featuring contributions from her vibrant creative community including Madison Cunningham, Kenneth Pattengale \(The Milk Carton Kids\), Sean Watkins \(Nickel Creek\), Rob Moose, Harrison Whitford, Hayden Everett, Drew Taubenfeld and many more, the record reflects Clearwater’s belief that music is something handmade, shared, and meant to be lived with. Available now on vinyl, CD, and streaming. https://www.instagram.com/lucyclearwater/ https://www.lucyclearwater.com/ https://lucyclearwater.bandcamp.com/

events.summary: The Bylines are a Portland based band created by Reece Marshburn and Marianna Thielen who write and perform sophisticated, jazz-inspired, story-driven pop music. They tour the Northwest regularly as a duo, and put on theatrical shows with their full ensemble. They are alumni of the Johnny Mercer Songwriters Project and have played before Randy Newman. Portland's The Bylines exists in a unique musical plane, one at once grounded in the big-band past of glamorous pop performances and rooted in a present realm of intricate and highly addictive songwriting. With a focus on grand live spectacle--a facet of music often lost in the digital age--the group is equally at home in velvet-curtained jazz halls, large rooms and intimate venues. That sound is the product of a marriage both sonic and literal. The Bylines is made up of two songwriters whose styles and influences converge to bring The Bylines' catchy, addictive sounds to vibrant life. Frontwoman Marianna Thielen, the glamorous face of the group, brings to the fore a background in composition, classical vocal work and, most obviously, musical theater, illuminating the stage with endlessly watchable bravado backed up by her powerful -- yet playful -- vocal prowess. Meanwhile, gliding his fingers across the keys is Reece Marshburn, letting loose a symphony of intricate melodies rooted in a combination of classical, jazz and pop music. The resulting combination is a unique pop confection drawing on decades of influences, as if Cole Porter, Carole King, Dusty Springfield, Freddie Mercury, Paul Simon, Rufus Wainwright and Regina Spektor combined forces and filtered their unique compositions through classical maestros and film composers, then sprinkled it with a keen pop sensibility and a commitment to putting on the most involving, charismatic and personalized live shows this side of the Copacabana. The Bylines have used their unique-yet-familiar sound to play to audiences large and small throughout the country, and have released both a studio\(self titled, recorded by Bob Stark at Kung Fu Bakery\) and a live album\(The Bylines Live, recorded at the Alberta Rose Theatre in Portland, OR\). The Bylines are proud alumni of the Johnny Mercer Songwriting Project, and have had support from the Regional Arts and Culture Council. Whether performing as a Thielen/Marshburn duo or with a larger band, the result is a blend of butter-smooth melodies, densely layered songwriting and powerful vocals. Most importantly, though, The Bylines musical cocktail goes down easy, and emphasizes something that is so often forgotten when such prolific songwriters present their craft: listening to music is, above all, supposed to be an experience… and a fun one.
events.title: The Bylines

events.summary: Every so often, you’re sitting at a bus stop or browsing at the cheese counter, and you stumble into an interaction. For a moment, you connect with a random person, having a brief conversation you didn’t know was coming. You get a glimpse of a world recombined into something foreign but familiar. Through that chance encounter and surprise conversation, you might find yourself reminded of other ways to live your own life. Life Recording — Live! illuminates the worlds of the people in the audience that night. Each month, interviewer Leif Olsen leverages their playfulness and curiosity to encourage a few members of the audience to talk about themselves for a while. The remaining audience listens and learns from the gems and insights of people living lives different from their own. Next time you find yourself out in the world of strangers, you might look for storytellers instead. Meet the team: Leif Olsen, The Life Recording Company, has been working with audio for a decade and has over 1.92 million views on their work across platforms. Leif has a Master's in Multimedia Journalism and has been recording people's life stories since 2019. Check out their work or book a life recording session at theliferecording.com Brandon Giles, is a producer and strategic planner who turns ambitious ideas into retreats, workshops, and events that engage people in inclusive, immersive ways. Through their business, LB Collaborations, Brandon facilitates collaboration for individuals and teams. Currently taking on new collaborations and strategic planning projects for fall 2026–more at bytheLB.Co Social Good Place offers co-working memberships, event spaces, and community events to create positive experiences and influences in our world. We also offer a pathway to fiscal sponsorship for charitable initiatives through our parent organization, Social Good Fund. Learn more at SocialGoodPlace.org Accessibility Note: Social Good Place is housed in a historic building with significant physical limitations. There is no level entry to the building, no ramps, and no elevators. Accessing the event space requires navigating stairs. You can read Social Good Place's full statement on accessibility at socialgoodplace.org.

For more than 20 years, award-winning virtuosos Terry Robb, Mark Hanson, and Doug Smith have captivated audiences with world-class fingerstyle guitar performances that blend blues, Hawaiian slack key, reggae, and beloved classics into a rich and unforgettable musical experience. This special holiday performance features stunning arrangements from their acclaimed recording O Christmas Three, alongside audience favorites and inventive new works, including Hanson’s sparkling ukulele version of “Santa Claus Is Coming to Town,” Robb’s playful jazz-inspired original “Santa Claus Owes Me Money,” and Smith’s masterful arrangement of “Waltz of the Flowers” from The Nutcracker. events.summary: Mason Jennings is a Minnesota-based pop-folk singer-songwriter. Jennings is originally from Honolulu, Hawaii. He is well known for his simple yet catchy melodies, intimate lyrics, intensely literary and historical themes, and deep tenor's voice. His music has appeared in the surf film Shelter and he has toured extensively. Jennings is married to Amy Jennings \(nee Turany\) and has a son, August, born in January 2003. Jennings produced his self-titled debut album in 1997 on an analog four-track in the basement of a rented home, manning all instruments himself. In October 1998, after bringing drummer Chris Stock and bassist Robert Skoro on board, he began a weekly gig at Minneapolis' 400 Bar as the Mason Jennings Band. Garnering local praise and a wide fan base, Mason began touring nationally. His 2000 album Birds Flying Away revealed Jennings' political activism and penchant for singing first-person narratives of imaginary rustic characters. Following the release of this album, Noah Levy took over drumming duties from Stock. 2002 saw the release of two albums: the studio piece Century Spring and a "fans only" collection of acoustic rarities, Simple Life. An EP supporting Century Spring was also released, featuring the album's opening track, "Living In The Moment," two live tracks, and the previously-unreleased "Emperor Ashoka." Jennings released all three discs -- and re-released his earlier albums -- on his homebrewed record label, Architect Records. In 2003, Skoro and Levy left the band \(the former to pursue a solo career\), and were replaced by bassist Chris Morrissey \(formerly of Bill Mike Band\) and drummer Brian Mcleod. On 10 February 2004, Jennings released Use Your Voice, which notably included the songs "Keepin' It Real," a foot-stomper ostensibly written at the request of Shrek 2 producers \(but not used in the film\), and "The Ballad of Paul and Sheila," an acoustic dirge for late Minnesota senator Paul Wellstone. On the 30th, September of that year, the band released a DVD entitled Use Your Van, which chronicled the recording of Use Your Voice and part of the promotional tour. The DVD was filmed by Andy Grund. On June 17, 2005, news broke that Jennings had finally signed with a major label: Glacial Pace, a subsidiary of Sony's Epic Records headed by Modest Mouse frontman Isaac Brock. Minnesota's Star Tribune broke the story, and credited Brock with convincing Jennings to sign after the Mason Jennings Band had opened for several Modest Mouse shows in 2004. Jennings had long avoided the major labels, citing desires to maintain creative control and dodge big-label politics. Jennings recorded his sixth album, "Boneclouds," at Pachyderm Studio in Cannon Falls, MN. The album was released on May 16, 2006 by Glacial Pace. After considerable success on "Boneclouds", Jennings released his seventh full length album "In the Ever". The album was released under Jack Johnson's "Brushfire Records".
events.title: Mason Jennings

events.summary: TICKETS ️ truewest.info/Pokey26 On Sale Friday, May 15 at 10am PT This Event is All Ages ---------------------------------------- Pokey LaFarge For two decades, Pokey LaFarge has walked his own effortlessly cool road as an exceptionally iconoclastic troubadour – forthright, genuine, and markedly keen to put it all out there. Rent Money now sees him pushing forward yet again in what can be safely declared his finest collection to date, both as an heartfelt expression of personal experience and as no-nonsense social commentary. With its twanging guitars, plucky rhythms, and undeniably captivating melodies, the album soars and swings, its joyous refrains belying the inescapable undercurrent of constant worry and angst that permeates these troubled times. As always, the Illinois native deftly traverses the genre boundaries, seamlessly integrating the myriad strains of 20th-century American music with a freewheeling command of earnest songcraft, inspired performance, and subversive creativity. Rent Money stands tall as an indisputable high-water mark for Pokey LaFarge – a defining collection from a one-of-a-kind artist of rare ingenuity and uncommon candor, now as ever, determinedly crafting a sure-footed brand of deeply human music all his own. “People are always going to tell you what they think you should play,” says Pokey LaFarge, “what you should sing about, how you should sound, how you should look, how you should act. And I’ve always just been like, nah. Nope. I’ve just completely gone my own way, and hopefully I’ve been honest and authentic in the process. “I’m just trying to make music that AI can’t replicate. Things are so homogenized right now. That’s what I’m really, really, really resistant to, especially when it comes to music. I’m not going to do it. I’m not going to conform.” Cicada Rhythm Born and raised in Georgia, this talented pair imitates and modernizes folk music to a rejuvenating degree. The sound of Andrea DeMarcus and Dave Kirslis exhibits skilled and articulate guitar picking honed in the dive bars of Atlanta over rolling Julliard-trained bass lines. Expect chilling harmonies, unbridled enthusiasm, some wholesome tunes and a sincere performance
events.title: Pokey LaFarge w/ Cicada Rhythm

events.summary: TICKETS truewest.info/Carlisle26 On Sale Tuesday, July 21 at 9am PT This Event is 21\+ ---------------------------------------- With a heavy-duty catalog of new material for a career first double album, The Universal Bubba marks a half dozen releases for folksinger Willi Carlisle and reaches new heights with the added accelerant of first time producer Tyler Childers. In an all-time DIY effort, Childers and his band convened to a makeshift home studio nestled in the Bywater District of New Orleans for two weeks to cut 17 tracks that expand Carlisle’s sonic scrapbook and capture the off-kilter characters living in his songs. “I think this one goes to outer space,” says Carlisle. “I think this is the widest range of influences that I’ve ever had. It touches on funk, it touches on Americana, Cajun, oldtime, and experimental music.” With Childers’ band behind him, Carlisle embraced the freedom to wander across genres both familiar and new, testing out instrumentation and toying with the surreality of traditions being turned on their head. “It feels like getting drunk at the Civil War reenactment, or cruising at the cattle auction, or doing molly at the square dance,” says Carlisle. “It’s the first time I’ve ever used synthesizers and double electric guitars. There’s also more fretless 19th century style banjo on it than any record I’ve ever made.” Exploration aside, Carlisle’s mission as a folksinger largely remains the same - documenting the stories and struggles of the people and balancing the humor and hope of existence. “I want to make a universal folk music. Songs for all kinds of weirdos,” says Carlisle. “With the idea that there is nobody that doesn’t have folk songs and everyone deserves folk songs. I want to write songs that prove the old weird America didn’t go anywhere, that we are living and dying for it everyday. I believe there’s noble work to do in that context. That if we feel despair, we don’t need to because there’s so much good work to do.”
events.title: Willi Carlisle - The Universal Bubba Tour

events.summary: Decades after her first fabled Nutcracker fever dream, Clara, no longer the child she once was, finds herself once again tumbling into a world of wonderment. Step into a holiday where tradition is turned upside down and inside out. ’Twas the Night Before Nutcracker is a glittering, whimsical journey through Clara’s holiday eve. What begins with a lively soirée and an innocent absinthe toast unravels into a dreamscape of marching soldiers, mischievous mice, swirling snowflakes, and sugarplum visions. Set to Can Can’s original adaptation of the iconic Nutcracker score, the show features new original songs alongside beloved holiday classics, a festive script, magical choreography, and stunning visuals. The spectacle weaves together classic, modern, aerial, and burlesque performances with Can Can’s refined cabaret style. Sprinkle in the perfect amount of comedy, and a touch of theatrical spark, and you’ve got a show as enchanting as it is unexpected. With its blend of elegance, humor, high kicks, and holiday spirit, ‘Twas the Night Before Nutcracker is a new holiday tradition in the making.
events.title: Can Can's 'Twas the Night Before Nutcracker

events.summary: Let's plant trees together in SE Vancouver! Interested in receiving a tree? Click HERE to purchase a tree for your household. Dozens of large \(6-10' tall\) trees will be ready for planting in their new homes, and your help is what makes this community planting possible! Please arrive by 8:45am to sign-in and be assigned a planting crew. The planting starts at 9:00am. We provide gloves, tools, and guidance, as well as light breakfast snacks and coffee/tea/hot chocolate. We ask that all volunteers dress for the weather, wear sturdy shoes/boots you don't mind getting dirty, and be ready to have fun! How do I register? Register by filling out this quick form . Groups, families, and individuals welcome! If your group is more than 5 people, please know you will be assigned to different planting crews. Have a pickup truck? We need your help getting these young trees to their planting sites a few blocks away from the central staging site. Please sign up if you're able to help out in this key role. Under age 18? We request that youth 15 and under volunteer with a parent/guardian. Youth 16 and older can volunteer on their own and will need to hand us a youth waiver form signed by their parent/guardian. Private transportation: You will travel from the meeting location to a few planting sites in the nearby neighborhood \(up to several miles\). We recommend private transportation \(bike or vehicle\), but there may be an option to carpool if others in your small planting crew are also comfortable with this. Where will these trees be planted? In the following neighborhoods: Bella Vista, Bennington, Cascade Highlands, Cascade Southeast, Columbia River, East Mill Plain, Fairway/164th, Fishers Creek, Fishers Landing East, Lewis & Clark Woods, View, Riveridge, Village at Fisher's Landing, and Wildwood. Questions? Please check out our Volunteer FAQ webpage . Our team is also happy to assist! Volunteer@friendsoftrees.org volunteer@friendsoftrees.org / 503-595-0213 We look forward to planting together soon! This event is in partnership with the City of Vancouver.
events.title: SE Vancouver neighborhood planting (Vancouver, WA)

events.summary: Join Friends of Trees for some planting fun with the City of Beaverton. You'll be planting native trees and shrubs along Fanno Creek Greenway! Fanno Creek is an urban stream that begins in Portland's SW hills and meanders 15 miles through neighborhoods in Portland, Beaverton, Tigard, and Durham, until it meets the Tualatin River. It is unique for being the only watershed drainage which falls within the boundaries of all three of our major metropolitan counties \(Multnomah, Washington & Clackamas\). Please arrive by 8:45am to sign-in and be assigned a planting crew. The planting starts at 9:00am. We provide gloves, tools, and planting guidance, as well as breakfast snacks and coffee/tea/hot chocolate -- all you need to do is show up dressed for the weather wearing sturdy shoes or boots, and be ready to have fun! events.summary: Vogue-published photographer Kenji Shimizu, Grammy-nominated producer and artist rei mastrogiovanni, and doctoral candidate in Japanese literature Teppei Fukuda together crafted this selection of photographs that portray Oregon’s four seasons through a critical reimagining of Japanese seasonal aesthetics. Drawing on the visual techniques of sumi-e ink painting, the five sets of photographs express seasonality through portraiture, gesture, everyday objects, and atmosphere. At the same time, the artists are exploring the relationship between tradition and cultural identity as Japanese and multi-heritage Japanese artists living in Oregon, superimposing one of the most prevalent motifs in Japanese art onto a new context. The individual artists’ works will also be on display, as well as artwork from the museum’s collection.
events.title: refractiv Photography Exhibition

events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. Plan your visit and explore the exhibition: worldforestry.org/lookout-landscape
events.title: Lookout Landscape Exhibition

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Explore the flavors of home with culinary expert Anna in a Chinese cooking demonstration featuring simple, authentic dishes. 11 AM – 12:30 PM | Every 2nd Saturday, May 23 – December 12, 2026 Food in Chinese culture is more than nourishment—it is culture, history, and a vital medium for social connection, care, and love. It plays an essential role in both festive celebrations and everyday life. We warmly invite you to join this Chinese cooking demonstration led by culinary expert Anna. She will demonstrate how to use locally sourced ingredients to create simple, authentic homestyle dishes that capture the true flavors of home. Get Admission Featured at the event: The Asian Food Pantry \(AFP\) Cookbook — a culturally inspired collection of recipes using ingredients commonly distributed through the pantry over the past six years. Cookbooks will be available for purchase, with all proceeds supporting the Asian Food Pantry and its work serving low-income Asian seniors in our community. Meet the Demonstrator: Anna Xu is a passionate baker and home cook, known for her expertise in traditional Shanghainese cuisine as well as Western pastries. She is the author of The Taste of Home, Where The Heart Belongs 家的味道，心的归属, a bi-lingual cookbook that celebrates the emotional connections we build through food and a fundraising initiative that supports the pantry’s mission. Anna also leads the Asian Food Pantry program at the Community for Positive Aging \(Hollywood Senior Center\), where she supports low-income Asian seniors by providing culturally familiar foods and fostering community connection. A longtime volunteer at Lan Su Chinese Garden, Anna is deeply committed to promoting and preserving Chinese culture through her work and community engagement. Parking & Directions Free Lan Su Parking There is free first come, first served parking in our sister lot next to the garden at 424 NW Third Avenue. Additional metered parking and garages are available on surrounding streets.

You’ll also learn a practical “First Aid” technique that can be used to support pain relief and encourage the body’s natural healing processes, along with simple methods to help reduce stress and promote calm. The class includes a short presentation introducing simplified subtle energy healing, followed by guided, hands-on practice. You’ll have the opportunity to practice scanning and energy techniques with pets while receiving guidance and feedback. Even if you don’t feel or see energy right away, that’s completely normal—these techniques are designed to be accessible and effective for beginners. You’re welcome to attend whether or not you bring an animal companion. Everyone interested in learning how to support animal wellness is invited to join. Registration is $55. Come learn practical tools you can use to support the health, comfort, and happiness of the animals you love. Well behaved dogs only please. events.summary: Kevin Watson is an Oregon singer-songwriter whose work blends the rugged Americana spirit of the Pacific Northwest with the timeless story telling of classic folk. Drawing inspiration from artists like Sturgill Simpson, Townes Van Zant, and Gillian Welch, Watson is also heavily influenced by late ‘60s and early 70’s rock. His songwriting hints at the people and places that shaped him along his unique journey - from professional athlete to independent recording artist, and everything in between. Along the way he developed a style that stretches from bluesy/country rock to folky fingerpicking. Whether backed by his full band or performing solo, Watson’s music delivers a sound that feels raw, weathered, and unshakably honest. His 2025 debut album ‘troubadour’ along with his most recent follow up singles ‘Ain’t Got Time’, released June 12th, and ‘Gone Again’, released September 4th, 2026, continue to showcase an artist committed to honest songwriting, memorable melodies, and music built to endure.

events.summary: The Bylines are a Portland based band created by Reece Marshburn and Marianna Thielen who write and perform sophisticated, jazz-inspired, story-driven pop music. They tour the Northwest regularly as a duo, and put on theatrical shows with their full ensemble. They are alumni of the Johnny Mercer Songwriters Project and have played before Randy Newman. Portland's The Bylines exists in a unique musical plane, one at once grounded in the big-band past of glamorous pop performances and rooted in a present realm of intricate and highly addictive songwriting. With a focus on grand live spectacle--a facet of music often lost in the digital age--the group is equally at home in velvet-curtained jazz halls, large rooms and intimate venues. That sound is the product of a marriage both sonic and literal. The Bylines is made up of two songwriters whose styles and influences converge to bring The Bylines' catchy, addictive sounds to vibrant life. Frontwoman Marianna Thielen, the glamorous face of the group, brings to the fore a background in composition, classical vocal work and, most obviously, musical theater, illuminating the stage with endlessly watchable bravado backed up by her powerful -- yet playful -- vocal prowess. Meanwhile, gliding his fingers across the keys is Reece Marshburn, letting loose a symphony of intricate melodies rooted in a combination of classical, jazz and pop music. The resulting combination is a unique pop confection drawing on decades of influences, as if Cole Porter, Carole King, Dusty Springfield, Freddie Mercury, Paul Simon, Rufus Wainwright and Regina Spektor combined forces and filtered their unique compositions through classical maestros and film composers, then sprinkled it with a keen pop sensibility and a commitment to putting on the most involving, charismatic and personalized live shows this side of the Copacabana. The Bylines have used their unique-yet-familiar sound to play to audiences large and small throughout the country, and have released both a studio\(self titled, recorded by Bob Stark at Kung Fu Bakery\) and a live album\(The Bylines Live, recorded at the Alberta Rose Theatre in Portland, OR\). The Bylines are proud alumni of the Johnny Mercer Songwriting Project, and have had support from the Regional Arts and Culture Council. Whether performing as a Thielen/Marshburn duo or with a larger band, the result is a blend of butter-smooth melodies, densely layered songwriting and powerful vocals. Most importantly, though, The Bylines musical cocktail goes down easy, and emphasizes something that is so often forgotten when such prolific songwriters present their craft: listening to music is, above all, supposed to be an experience… and a fun one.

events.summary: Everything is driven by sheer curiosity and loose, if any, creative parameters, the band says. A person’s twenties is guaranteed to be a tumultuous time in their life anyway, regardless of who they are or what they do, but the members of Robber Robber found themselves in a world that’s maybe never been more chaotic or difficult to move through. It’s a chaos that’s evident in what they create, even if it’s only the obstacle they’re reacting to. In even their most polarizing musical moments, you get the sense that these are gut reactions being expressed, that truth is the grist of the overflow.

events.summary: Take a pause from the everyday and spend an evening connecting with yourself, the moon, and the people around you. Join Danie Rhodes at Breathing Room for a candlelit New Moon Ceremony. Through astrology, guided meditation, intentional ritual, and time in community, we’ll explore the themes of this moon and what they might bring up for you. No experience with astrology or moon ceremonies is needed. Just come as you are, bring an open mind, and make a little room for yourself. Together, we’ll explore: Moon & Astrology - Learn about the themes of the full moon and how they may connect to your own life. Guided Meditation - Slow down, settle in, and make space to listen inward. Intentional Ritual - Reflect on what you’re ready to release, what you want to nurture, and what you’re making room for next. Cards & Reflection - Work with oracle cards for personal insight, inspiration, and a fresh perspective. Crystal Intention - Connect with the symbolism and energy of crystals, and take a specially chosen stone home with you. Community & Connection - Share space with others in a welcoming, candlelit setting, with room for conversation, reflection, or simply being present. Leave with a little more clarity, a renewed sense of intention, and time well spent with yourself and your community. About Danie: Danie Rhodes is a certified Spiritual Wellness Practitioner, Holistic Health Coach, and Intuitive Tarot Reader with a deep love for astrology, the moon, and the ways we can reconnect with ourselves. Through moon ceremonies, she weaves together astrological insight, guided meditation, intentional ritual, tarot and oracle cards, and the grounding energy of crystals to create space for reflection, connection, and personal growth. Her gatherings invite you to slow down, set intentions, release what no longer serves you, and reconnect with your own inner wisdom in community.
events.title: New Moon in Sagittarius Ceremony

Alvarez's gloriously unhinged Christmas comedy is exactly what it sounds like; A Christmas Carol. Rudolph. It's a Wonderful Life. The Grinch. events.summary: At the height of the holiday season, a group of workers and their families discover that their wages are going to be cut. Together, they decide to fight for a better life. As the struggle drags on, they find joy and community through the music and stories of their different traditions….and of this new world they now share. Featuring early 20th century American classics, alongside songs and folktales from Eastern Europe, Italy, the Philippines, and the Latin American diaspora, Bread and Roses celebrates the tapestry of people who helped to build this country, proclaiming "We all deserve joy, We all deserve beauty!" Portland Revels' annual holiday Midwinter Revels production celebrates the winter solstice and the return of the light at the darkest time of year. Each season the production is set in a different place and time, allowing us to explore different cultures and music traditions, while grounding the show in our familiar rituals and themes.
events.title: Portland Revels presents "Bread and Roses"

events.summary: ⭐️ Single tickets go on sale December 15, but you can reserve your tickets now with a season subscription! ⭐️ Sylvia Ridge, Tennessee is known for one thing during the holiday season: their Christmas pageant. When Oralene, the guiding force behind the production suddenly passes away, the tight-knit group of women she left behind—known as the Silver Belles—must step up to save the show. As they fumble through rehearsals and face old wounds, they rediscover their voices, their strength, and their deep bond with one another. With twangy new country tunes, holiday classics, and plenty of Southern charm, "The Silver Belles" rings in the season with community and the kind of chosen family that helps us find our place—even when we feel a little lost. Book by Allyson Currin Music by Matt Conner Lyrics by Stephen Gregory Smith Based on an idea by Cathy Alter & Sandra Johnson On stage November 25 – December 20, 2026 Performances held at the Broadway Rose New Stage, 12850 SW Grant Avenue, Tigard, OR Title Sponsor: Harvey & Sandy Platt Show Sponsor: CTA Pathology
events.title: The Silver Belles

events.summary: A John Prine Christmas with Jenner Fox Band Saturday, December 12th @ 7:30pm Doors open at 7:00 pm www.jennerfoxband.com Ever wonder what John Prine has to do with Christmas? Ever wished the beloved songwriter had more to do with sleigh bells, eggnog, and Old Saint Nick. Well, in 1994 Prine released his 11th LP titled, “A John Prine Christmas.” The critics didn’t acclaim it much, but with titles such as “Silent Night All Day Long '' and “I Saw Mommy Kissing Santa Claus,” it’s still Prine at his lovely wry best, bringing Christmas home. We are proud to present “A John Prine Christmas” – a night of your favorite songs featuring folk troubadour and Prine scholar, Jenner Fox, with his all-star band. The evening will weave together Prine’s classic hits, his holiday themed songs, stories, and lots of singing along. Come prepared to laugh and cry and ho ho ho your way through celebrating a true American original. The Bellingham, WA based band features piano, electric guitar, bass, acoustic guitar, and rich vocal harmonies. $35 - Adults $30 - Seniors/Students $5 - Arts for All - Anyone with an Oregon Trail Card
events.title: A John Prine Christmas with the Jenner Fox Band - A Nostalgic Tribute

Doors: 7:00pmShow: 8:00pm Ages 21+.Step Into GVA!!!! - Genevieve Artadis New Anime-Inspired RecordTeleport into Genevieve Artadis supersonic universe with her newanime-inspired record, GVA!!!!!Channeled by the kinetic energy of her anime favorites from Naruto, Bleach, Initial D, Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood, Jojos Bizarre Adventures, Rurouni Kenshin and Attack on Titan Artadis fifth album is my dedication to anime.Speaking on the albums inspiration, Artadi describes, The inspiration I felt was like being turned inside out, like some dormant dreams could awaken in a really fun and creative way. It was great to feel driven like this instead of getting pulverized by the worlds increasing grayness. Of course this would come out in my music and in a twisted kind of way.The album continues her signature fusion of experimental jazz with indie punk, dream pop, alt-electronic, cinematic ballads, and lush harmonic writing, but it is Genevieves voice and arrangements that crystallizes her beautiful expression into a future-sonic world that is truly her own. GVA!!!! is brought to life with her collaborators: Louis Cole, Pedro Martins, Justin Brown, Daryl Johns, Sam Wilkes, Chiquita Magic, Chris Fishman, and Miku Nakamura (of C shu Nie). GVA!!!!! is an energetic, rocking, colorful record through which I hope to bring a sense of ignition to peoples souls who hear it, explains Artadi.Out on all platforms this October 30, follow the release with her anime-inspired retro music videos and live tour dates with Louis Cole and Chiquita Magic.

events.summary: Decades after her first fabled Nutcracker fever dream, Clara, no longer the child she once was, finds herself once again tumbling into a world of wonderment. Step into a holiday where tradition is turned upside down and inside out. ’Twas the Night Before Nutcracker is a glittering, whimsical journey through Clara’s holiday eve. What begins with a lively soirée and an innocent absinthe toast unravels into a dreamscape of marching soldiers, mischievous mice, swirling snowflakes, and sugarplum visions. Set to Can Can’s original adaptation of the iconic Nutcracker score, the show features new original songs alongside beloved holiday classics, a festive script, magical choreography, and stunning visuals. The spectacle weaves together classic, modern, aerial, and burlesque performances with Can Can’s refined cabaret style. Sprinkle in the perfect amount of comedy, and a touch of theatrical spark, and you’ve got a show as enchanting as it is unexpected. With its blend of elegance, humor, high kicks, and holiday spirit, ‘Twas the Night Before Nutcracker is a new holiday tradition in the making.

events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. Plan your visit and explore the exhibition: worldforestry.org/lookout-landscape
events.title: Lookout Landscape Exhibition

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Vogue-published photographer Kenji Shimizu, Grammy-nominated producer and artist rei mastrogiovanni, and doctoral candidate in Japanese literature Teppei Fukuda together crafted this selection of photographs that portray Oregon’s four seasons through a critical reimagining of Japanese seasonal aesthetics. Drawing on the visual techniques of sumi-e ink painting, the five sets of photographs express seasonality through portraiture, gesture, everyday objects, and atmosphere. At the same time, the artists are exploring the relationship between tradition and cultural identity as Japanese and multi-heritage Japanese artists living in Oregon, superimposing one of the most prevalent motifs in Japanese art onto a new context. The individual artists’ works will also be on display, as well as artwork from the museum’s collection.
events.title: refractiv Photography Exhibition

events.summary: About the event ReClaim It’s annual winter pop-up fundraiser, Holiday Shop 2026, is a celebration of local creativity and sustainable gift giving!
